#1911. Man United, Arsenal handed huge early suspension boosts after Igor Thiago VAR decision

By Ben Knapton | 08 Nov 2026 14:46, Last updated: 08 Nov 2026 15:02

Manchester United and Arsenal have been handed huge early boosts for their Premier League clashes with Brentford, which Igor Thiago will miss through suspension.

The Brazil international started up top for the Bees in their trip to Brighton & Hove Albion, but things quickly unravelled for Keith Andrews's side at the Amex Stadium.

Brentford fell 1-0 down within 15 minutes to a Diego Gomez goal, before Thiago and Chema Andres were involved in a set-to, which saw Thiago shove the Brighton man in the face.

The striker was initially booked for his role in the incident, but upon reviewing the incident on the pitchside monitor, referee Michael Oliver issued a straight red card to Thiago.

"After review, Brentford No.9 pushes his opponent in the face with force. Yellow card is cancelled and the final decision is red card," Oliver announced to the crowd, as Thiago prepares to serve a three-game suspension.

Brentford are a goal down and now a man down ? Igor Thiago is sent off after a VAR review. Referee Michael Oliver says he pushed Brighton's Chema Andres "in the face with force." https://t.co/YMZrYFUGyx

As the Brentford man was dismissed for violent conduct, he will be forced to sit out the Bees' next three matches against Everton, Man United and Arsenal after the international break.

Thiago begins his ban against Everton on November 23, before Andrews's men travel to Man United on November 28, and he completes his suspension against champions Arsenal on December 2.

The 25-year-old's punishment could be revoked if Brentford are successful with an appeal, but it is extremely unlikely that the Bees would win their case if they decided to contest the decision.

Andrews will therefore have to cope without his chief centre-forward for crunch clashes with Arsenal and Man Utd, although Thiago has so far struggled to replicate his 22-goal form from 2025-26.

The South American has scored just two goals and set up two more in 10 Premier League games this season, although each one of those contributions came in his last five full appearances.

Thiago's absence is especially untimely for Brentford, as Andrews is also working without another striker - 19-year-old Kaye Furo - due to a serious foot injury.

Furo has made "really good progress" in his recuperation, though, and there is a chance that the 2007-born striker could be ready for competitive action following the international break.

However, Thiago's ban could instead open the door for 34-year-old veteran Callum Wilson to make his first Premier League starts of the season, as the Englishman has made just six substitute appearances in the 2026-27 English top flight so far.

Dango Ouattara and Kevin Schade could also be deployed as auxiliary centre-forwards, but Thiago's absence nevertheless represents a major blow for Brentford, and a major boost for Arsenal and Man Utd.

#1907. Alisson reveals transfer plan with Liverpool contract set to expire

Alisson Becker has revealed that he wants to stay at Liverpool, despite his contract on Merseyside expiring this summer.

#1905. Paul Merson says Arsenal star has been ‘like a new signing’ after Hull win

Paul Merson reserved special praise for Martin Odegaard following Arsenal’s gritty 1-0 victory over Hull City, claiming the midfielder has been ‘like a new signing’ this season.

Arsenal had looked on course to drop points for only the second time this term as newly promoted Hull dug in and managed to frustrate their hosts, with Declan Rice coming close to breaking the deadlock on three occasions.

Noni Madueke also had his head in his hands after being denied by Konstantinos Tzolakis with the minutes ticking down in front of an increasingly agitated Emirates crowd.

But the pressure told with 18 minutes remaining of normal time as Tzolakis again kept out Madueke, only for Odegaard to pounce and poke the ball home on the rebound to cue rapturous scenes in north London.

The reigning Premier League champions preserved their narrow advantage to ensure they moved six points clear at the top of the table after Manchester City were stunned in a 3-1 defeat away to Nottingham Forest.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

High-flying Brighton – the only team to get the better of Arsenal – will look to close the gap to five points when they play host to Brentford later this afternoon.

‘You know Hull are going to sit ten behind the ball and make it very difficult,’ ex-Arsenal and England midfielder Merson said of Arsenal’s win over Hull on Sky Sports.

‘If you score early, you just go on and then win 3-0 or 4-0 and it would be a nice day at the office. That didn’t happen.

‘Hull defended very well and it took Martin Odegaard to break them down if I’m being honest.

‘Noni Madueke comes inside, hits a shot, it gets parried… he’s the first one to react and there’s two defenders in front of him, about four or five yards in front of him, but because of his reaction, he runs past them, he hits it, there’s a slight deflection and it goes underneath the goalkeeper’s arms.’

Merson felt Hull shot-stopper Tzolakis was the man of the match in a game which could later be seen as vital if Arsenal are to successfully defend their title this season.

He added: ‘Arsenal weren’t great but they won and this could be one of those games you look back on at the end of the season and go, “Remember the Hull game when we nicked it at the end”, but yeah, Hull will come away and think they did alright.

‘For me, the goalkeeper was the man of the match for Hull so that tells you everything. Arsenal weren’t great but it was a great result.’

Odegaard was once again the heartbeat of everything Arsenal did well to continue what has been an outstanding start to the 2026/27 campaign for the Gunners captain.

The crucial 72nd-minute strike took the Norwegian’s goalscoring tally to five in all competitions this season. He managed only one goal in 36 appearances last term.

‘He’s been outstanding. He’s the only one really that moves it quickly,’ Merson said of Odegaard.

‘He moves it quickly, he moves, he gets into positions. I just thought too many players took too many touches and they slowed it down and gave Hull half a chance.

‘I think he’s been outstanding this season, he’s like a new signing for them and he’s been the man so far.

‘Not great but just a good result for Arsenal. But again, he was one of the stars of the show.’

Arsenal will hope to tighten their vicelike grip on top spot when they return to Premier League action against Newcastle at St James’ Park in a week’s time.

A tough Champions League clash at home to Borussia Dortmund awaits three days later, before Mikel Arteta’s men head back to the Emirates to face off against Manchester City in the English top flight.

#1904. Arsenal sent clear new penalty verdict in call for law change

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal were denied a penalty against Hull after the officials incorrectly applied the laws of the game.

That is the view of former referee Dermot Gallagher, who said of the incident: “ethically it is right but by the laws it is wrong”.

The Gunners beat Hull 1-0 on Saturday thanks to Martin Odegaard’s second-half goal and will spend the international break sitting five points clear at the top of the Premier League.

However, there was a controversial moment in the first half at the Emirates Stadium when the score remained 0-0 and Arsenal were not awarded a penalty.

Referee Farai Hallam stopped play to go to the monitor and assess whether Nobel Mendy’s pull of Kai Havertz’s shirt in the box was a foul.

It was decided that while Havertz was fouled and the contact was worthy of a penalty, the Arsenal striker was offside and so a free-kick was given to Hull.

That went against the laws of the game, which say the offside should have been irrelevant as Havertz was not attempting to play the ball or challenging an opponent for it.

Gallagher believes that Arsenal should have been awarded a spot-kick, but expressed sympathy for the officials involved.

He claimed that “common sense” would suggest that Havertz was offside and so a penalty could not be awarded, as he called for the rules to be tweaked to avoid such confusion.

“The law says that if a player in an offside position is fouled before the offside occurs, a foul should be given and therefore a penalty,” Gallagher said on Sky Sports.

Choose the right education path for your child

“In law, you should give a penalty. It is quite clear, the foul occurred before. But we talk about common sense. Havertz is 100 per cent offside. His starting position is offside.

“Three things he can’t do: he can’t play the ball as he’d be interfering, he can’t challenge an opponent and he can’t go in front of the goalkeeper. He is offside and the net result should be a penalty.

“Common sense is not allowed. When you think of it morally, can you really give a penalty for a player who is never in an onside position? He can’t play the ball.

“The process of VAR was fantastic. The assistant calls offside the minute the ball comes in. The start position for the assistant was always offside.

“Ethically it is right but by law it is wrong. There is scope for tightening it up [the laws].”

#1902. Ipswich vs. Bournemouth: Evanilson makes history after shocking goalkeeper error

By Ben Knapton | 08 Nov 2026 15:12, Last updated: 08 Nov 2026 15:26

Evanilson etched his name into the Bournemouth history books by opening the scoring in Sunday's Premier League clash with Ipswich Town.

The Brazil international came into the Portman Road battle in hot goalscoring form, having netted in four top-flight games in succession.

However, Evanilson was gifted one of the easiest goals he will ever score in English football against Ipswich, thanks to a shocking mistake from Tractor Boys goalkeeper Christian Walton.

Under pressure from Evanilson, Walton attempted to drag the ball away from the Bournemouth striker rather than clearing his lines, but he was robbed of possession by the South American.

Evanilson evaded Walton's desperate sprawling grasp and slotted the ball into an empty net, thus becoming the first Bournemouth player in history to score in five straight Premier League games.

It's Evanilson again for Bournemouth! ? A nightmare for Christian Walton and Evanilson makes no mistake https://t.co/QYGU9Xaniv

The 27-year-old's scoring sequence began on October 10, when he netted the Cherries' consolation goal in their 5-1 hammering at the hands of Chelsea at Stamford Bridge.

Evanilson then found the net in each of his three remaining Premier League games in October, helping to propel Bournemouth to victory against Sunderland, Manchester United and Leeds United.

The Brazilian failed to score in any of his first five league appearances of the campaign, but he has now moved onto nine direct involvements from his first 10 games, having also chalked up four assists.

Evanilson has also registered three goal contributions from four Europa League games - two of his own and one assist - while managing 12 in total across 14 outings in all tournaments.

Following the South American's early opener, Bournemouth doubled their lead on the stroke of half time through a Leif Davis own goal, putting Marco Rose's men on the verge of a fourth successive Premier League victory.

By making the net bulge at Portman Road, Evanilson moved above Junior Stanislas into outright seventh place in Bournemouth's all-time Premier League scoring charts.

The Brazilian is now just one behind teammate Justin Kluivert and two adrift of Marcus Tavernier, who is the highest active scorer in the Cherries' squad with 23 to his name.

Dominic Solanke's 28 and Antoine Semenyo's 30 are also within reach for Evanilson this season, but the Brazilian may need to wait a while longer to surpass Callum Wilson's 41 or Josh King's unparalleled 48.

Eli Junior Kroupi is further down the list in 10th place, but the much-coveted Frenchman boasts the best goals-per-game ratio of any Bournemouth Premier League player with 0.37.

#1900. Josh King: Fulham star reveals England mentor after shock Nations League call-up by Thomas Tuchel

Fulham’s Josh King has revealed that Jude Bellingham has taken him under his wing for England, and insists he is willing to play wherever Thomas Tuchel needs him.

The attacking midfielder was called up to take part in the Three Lions’ pre-World Cup training camp in Florida in June but on Friday received his first proper call-up to the senior squad ahead of Nations League matches against Croatia on Thursday and Spain on Sunday.

While only 19, King has been given plenty of responsibility for his club under Alvaro Arbeloa this season and has been rewarded now with the chance to earn his senior international debut over the coming week.

“There were a lot of people I learned from [in the pre-World Cup camp].” King said.

“Jude was a big person for me. He took me under his wing and tried to make me feel welcome. There were a lot of players like that. Harry Kane as well, he was one person who really made me feel welcome and tried to help me through my time there.

“But it's a credit to what England have going here, everyone is a really good person as well as good player on the pitch.”

King added: “Playing for England is the dream so to be that one step closer is an amazing achievement, something I've been working towards for a long time. I'm grateful to the manager for putting his trust in me.”

Tuchel said on Friday that he had King as one of his options on the right wing this month, but sees him as able to play in a variety of attacking positions.

“I'm happy to play anywhere for the manager,” King said on Monday. “I have to add other parts to my game, in wider positions you might have to cover defensively or make runs in behind.

“I'm capable of playing lots of different positions, which is probably one of the reasons why I'm here.”

In an interview with Standard Sport in April, King said he wants to become “one of the best midfielders in the world” and dreams in time of being a “leader” for club and country.

#1898. Mikel Arteta admits Arsenal are struggling with familiar problem after Hull win

Mikel Arteta admits Arsenal are struggling with an old problem that became so cliched that it was featured in a sit-com 18 years ago.

The Gunners beat Hull City 1-0 on Saturday in the Premier League, with Martin Odegaard scoring the only goal at the Emirates.

Any problem Arsenal are struggling with is not too serious as that win, followed by Manchester City’s defeat at Nottingham Forest, put Arteta’s men six points clear at the top of the table.

However, Arteta was frustrated with Arsenal only scoring one goal and it not coming until the 72nd minute, despite dominating possession and producing 21 shots at goal.

Sometimes the inability to even produce a shot was the problem, despite having the ball in dangerous areas plenty of times.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

In a 2008 episode of The IT Crowd, Moss and Roy both try to ingratiate with football fans by learning the phrase: ‘The thing about Arsenal is they’re always trying to walk it in.’

Arteta seems to have a similar take on his team, accusing them of trying to score the ‘perfect goal’ against defensively-minded teams.

‘[We need to] be more efficient,’ the Arsenal manager said. ‘We are one against one against the keeper. That’s happened twice today. There is a penalty there, there is another situation inside the box where the ball is bouncing.

‘So many shots that have been deflected, blocked. We need to find ways to be more efficient, sometimes even more pragmatic.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘Sometimes my feeling is that we are trying to score a perfect goal against these low blocks. We need to be much more chaotic than that, and that’s it. And open, I think, the scoreline much earlier because obviously that’s going to change the course of the game.

‘We had enough chances to make the scoreline much bigger. We weren’t efficient enough to do that. And then we have to rely on generating volume, generating a lot of situations in and around the box, insisting, insisting and insisting until we are able to break them down. And this is exactly how we won the game.’

Odegaard is Arsenal’s top-scorer this season with five goals in all competitions and three in the Premier League.

While Arsenal’s attack does not always penetrate as much as Arteta would like, the defence is incredibly reliable.

Another clean sheet meant the Gunners have conceded just five goals in 10 league games and have not conceded in 10 of their 17 matches across all competitions.

Centre-back Gabriel Magalhaes said: ‘If we don’t concede goals, we have a big chance to win games. We are really happy to have another clean sheet.

‘Like I said, when we have a strong team, a strong defence, we don’t concede goals. I think this season, how many is that? Ten clean sheets in the whole competition? This is our standard. We need to keep winning.’

#1897. Liverpool sent new Dominik Szoboszlai injury update as statement issued

Liverpool midfielder Dominik Szoboszlai will be assessed on Monday to determine his fitness for international duty with Hungary.

Szoboszlai was forced off in the second half of the Reds’ 3-1 win at Crystal Palace in the Premier League on Sunday due to a knee complaint.

During the last international break, Szoboszlai aggravated an existing muscular issue in his thigh, later breaking down just half an hour into his comeback against Brentford as he ended up missing five matches in total.

The latest issue has led to doubts over his availability to play for Hungary in their upcoming Nations League matches against Georgia and Northern Ireland.

The Hungarian Football Federation (MLSZ) released a statement on Monday which read: “(Dominik Szoboszlai) who was substituted in the 69th minute of Liverpool FC's match yesterday, is undergoing tests today, Monday, following the usual protocol in such cases. We will, of course, keep the public informed of developments as soon as possible."

Andoni Iraola admitted that Szoboszlai was not fully fit and hoped that Liverpool would not lose more key players to injury during the latest international break.

“Dom definitely wasn’t 100 per cent in the second half,” the Reds boss said after the win at Selhurst Park. "Let’s see. The last thing we need now is to lose players in the international games.

"In the last international break we lost three very important players in Alex (Isak), Cody (Gakpo) and Dom. So now I'm praying - it's the last thing we need.”

Iraola offered insight into Szoboszlai’s latest issue, adding: “I think Dom extended the knee a little bit. It was fine but not 100 per cent. He has to be careful to see if he can play for the international team or not.

“I hope we are in a better place in two weeks. I know Dom will do everything to go as he loves to play for the national team, but he wasn’t 100 per cent when he finished the game.

#1896. ‘Time passes by’ – Mancini warns Zaniolo he must seize Italy chance

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Roberto Mancini has warned Nicolo Zaniolo that he must start taking his opportunities to impress for Italy, before time runs out for the playmaker.

Zaniolo has been included in the Azzurri's squad for their upcoming Nations League fixtures against France and Belgium, with their qualification from Group A1 still in the balance.

Having taken seven points from their opening four games, Italy sit second in the group, three points below France and one above Belgium, meaning their matchday six meeting with the Red Devils – in Brussels on Sunday – could be a winner-take-all clash.

Zaniolo was initially included in Mancini's first squad since returning to the Italy job in September, but a thigh issue caused the Udinese man to pull out.

The 27-year-old also struggled with a hamstring problem at the start of the campaign, restricting him to just six Serie A appearances in 2026-27.

He has scored one goal and provided one assist this season for Udinese, who he joined on loan last season before making his stay permanent in the summer, and it has been more than two years since he represented his country.

Once seen as a burgeoning talent for Roma and Italy, Zaniolo has only won 19 senior caps – 10 of which have come from the bench – with the most recent of those coming against Ecuador in March 2024.

Zaniolo's only two senior international goals came against Armenia in November 2019, and Mancini has warned he will not get many more chances to shine on the big stage.

"I expect the same thing as I do from everyone else – to perform well and be consistent," Mancini told reporters, when asked what he expected from Zaniolo.

"He must start being decisive, because time passes by. He used to be a kid, and now he should be a player who makes a difference for the national team."

"Back in 2018, we had more experienced players," he said.

"Giorgio [Chiellini], Leo [Bonucci], [Marco] Verratti, Jorginho… they were the most experienced ones. Today, we don't have many."

San Siro will be the venue for Italy's meeting with France on Thursday, with Les Bleus knowing a victory would secure top spot in the group.

Dan Burn has been added to the England squad as a replacement for the injured Marc Guehi ahead of Thursday’s match against Croatia.

The Three Lions face Croatia at Wembley Stadium in their penultimate Nations League group game, before completing their group-phase in Madrid against world champions Spain on Sunday.

Manchester City centre-back Guehi was assessed over the weekend after being substituted with a hip injury at half time of their defeat to Nottingham Forest but has now pulled out of the squad.

In his place, Thomas Tuchel called up the 34-year-old Newcastle defender. He had said on Friday that “difficult phone calls” had been had with Burn, Dean Henderson and Chelsea’s Jordan Henderson when leaving them behind. But the former is now in as Guehi’s replacement.

Captain Harry Kane is expected to start and will overtake Peter Shilton to become England’s all-time most-capped player.

Arsenal duo Bukayo Saka (injury) and Noni Madueke (selection decision) are not in the squad this month but the head coach has explained that he sees his options on the right wing as being Liverpool’s Rio Ngumoha, Chelsea’s Morgan Rogers, Nottingham Forest’s Morgan Gibbs-White and Fulham’s Josh King.

Declan Rice is back in the mix and available after missing the last international break due to load management.

Jobe Bellingham of Borussia Dortmund, brother of Real Madrid’s Jude, is in the squad for the very first time at senior level. He, King and the Brighton veteran goalkeeper Jason Steele are the only uncapped players among Tuchel’s squad.

The German is expected to go strong in both matches after revealing on Friday that it matters to him to push to finish top of their Nations League group despite currently trailing Spain by three points.

Tuchel has a choice to make between Jordan Pickford and James Trafford over to start as his goalkeeper. Both were handed two games each during the last extended international break.

#1890. Next Crystal Palace manager: Contenders to replace Pierre Sage as clear favourite emerges

Pierre Sage will be sacked as Crystal Palace manager following Sunday’s 3-1 home defeat by Liverpool.

The Frenchman’s job has been under serious scrutiny for weeks now, with Palace heading into the November international break sitting rock bottom of the Premier League table after winning just two and losing seven of their first 10 games this season.

Sage has struggled to get his ideas across since taking over from Oliver Glasner in the summer, having enjoyed a terrific campaign with Lens last term.

The Eagles have the worst defence in the Premier League with 24 goals conceded so far, and Sage has run out of time to convince Palace’s decision-makers that he is the right man for the job.

With an announcement on Sage’s future imminent, they have already sounded out potential replacements.

Standard Sport has assessed who could take over at Selhurst Park next...

Out of work since being sacked by Tottenham in February, Thomas Frank was one of several candidates that Palace looked at to succeed Glasner in the summer and is the early frontrunner to replace Sage.

Frank’s reputation is in need of rehabilitation, and it is unclear how much of a toll his torrid eight-month spell in charge of Spurs took, but he remains highly regarded after his work with Brentford.

Frank released a statement in June saying he was taking some time out of football before his next job, so the Dane may be unwilling to jump into a role so soon after the season has started.

Another manager who stepped away from football over the summer, Kieran McKenna made the shock decision to leave Ipswich after earning promotion back to the Premier League.

One of Britain’s most highly sought-after young coaches, McKenna’s decision to spend more time with his family came as a surprise, but potentially hints at the fact that he is not yet ready to get back into management.

McKenna’s patient, possession-based style would constitute a dramatic change in tactics for Palace, but the Northern Irishman is comfortable using a three-man defence when his team has the ball.

Bringing in former Newcastle boss Eddie Howe would be considered quite the coup for Palace.

The Englishman has attracted interest from Manchester United amid ongoing doubts over Michael Carrick’s future and guided Newcastle to Carabao Cup glory in 2025.

Howe is actively open to new opportunities, but is said to be willing to wait for an elite, high-profile job, which could leave Palace out of the running.

Arguably the most divisive name on the list, Sean Dyche’s pragmatic approach is a far cry from the expansive, counter-attacking football Palace fans have been used to under Glasner and, to a lesser extent, Sage.

Dyche’s Premier League experience, especially given that Palace will have one eye on ensuring they stay in the top-flight, makes him an attractive proposition for those in the boardroom.

Whether they would be prepared to face the inevitable backlash his appointment would prompt is a different question entirely, though.

Coventry boss Frank Lampard is reportedly under consideration for the Palace job despite signing only a new contract with the promoted Sky Blues in June.

Lampard is a long-standing target and one of several other candidates Palace are reportedly eyeing up alongside Kim Hellberg and Vitor Matos, who have led Middlesbrough and Swansea, respectively, towards the top of the Championship table this term.

Free agent Vitor Pereira is also said to be on Palace’s shortlist, while Australia head coach and former Palace captain Tony Popovic could be a surprise contender.

England assistant Anthony Barry is a risky but potentially intriguing appointment, while former Wolves boss Rob Edwards is well known to Palace sporting director Matt Hobbs.

By Matthew Cooper | 08 Nov 2026 15:35, Last updated: 08 Nov 2026 18:10

Barnet will be looking to secure their place in the EFL Trophy knockout stages when they welcome Leyton Orient to The Hive Stadium on Tuesday evening.

The hosts currently sit second in their group and are in prime position to reach the knockouts, while the visitors are third.

Barnet are enjoying an impressive season and are second in League Two with 26 points from their opening 13 matches, just five points behind leaders Salford City.

Dean Brennan's side are unbeaten in their last four games, having booked their place in the second round of the FA Cup on Saturday with a dramatic 3-0 victory over Tranmere Rovers.

As a result, Barnet will secure a spot in the knockouts simply by avoiding a heavy defeat against Leyton Orient.

Leyton Orient currently sit 14th in League One with 17 points from 13 matches, but they travel to north London with some real momentum after big wins in their last two games.

Richie Wellens's side beat Cambridge United 3-0 in the league before thumping Harborough Town 5-1 in the FA Cup and they will be keen to carry that momentum into Tuesday's clash.

In the EFL Trophy, Orient have collected just two points so far, having beaten Wimbledon on penalties after a 1-1 draw and losing 2-1 against Arsenal Under-21s.

The visitors are three points behind Barnet in the group and need a five-goal swing to overtake them on goal difference.

#1888. Amorim offers honest Milan reflection: “We’re not ready, we’re far from being a really strong team”

Ruben Amorim continued the criticism of his AC Milan side after their dismal defeat to Ferencvaros, branding them ‘not ready’ to compete on multiple fronts.

Amorim made the decision to enact six changes to the starting line-up from the team that beat Inter convincingly in the derby at the weekend, but it backfired as his team never got going last night and were well-beaten by the Hungarians.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It is reported that after the game the Portuguese coach gave a long speech to his players about their attitude and effort levels. Milan remain incredibly inconsistent on this front, as they continue to alternate very encouraging performances with disastrous and listless ones.

Amorim laid into his team during an interview with Sky after the final whistle, and then he spoke to the CBS Sports Golazo studio shortly afterwards. The exchange was transcribed by MilanNews.

Yesterday you were talking about identity, about character. Was this the difference?

“Yes, technically, tactically, and above all mentally, they were superior and deserved to win. Today we weren’t ready to play professional football, and I felt it. We need to look within ourselves and do better.”

And in the Champions League the level would be even higher…

“We have to focus on the small details, without thinking about the Champions League or anything like that. We just have to focus on improving the more specific aspects of football: the mentality, the heart, the passion. We have to improve on that.”

What is Ferencvaros’ level in European football, how do you rate them?

“I don’t know, it depends on the opponent, but they’re doing very well. They have four wins in four games, a clear identity, and today they were superior to us.”

What did this match tell you about Milan?

“That we’re not ready. We’re not ready, we’re far from being a really strong team. We have moments, in some games, where we’re really strong, but then we can’t maintain our level, especially mentally. So this game told me and all of us that we’re not ready to be a very strong team.”

During the first half, I noticed you were very energetic on the sidelines, and then it almost seemed like you stopped giving directions. Can you tell there’s a certain lack of understanding within the team and that they’re not playing the way you’d like?

“No, I just do what I feel at the time, and sometimes I don’t do certain things just for show. We didn’t play well, that’s for sure; we had a completely different attitude in the last league game, while today we weren’t mentally prepared to fight for the win, and that’s what we need to work on.”

If there hadn’t been the derby at the weekend, do you think this match would have gone better?

“I have no idea, it doesn’t matter. It doesn’t matter, we have to be ready to play every three days in different competitions. So it doesn’t matter if we had a match before or not. I think we have to improve a lot in all aspects of the game.”

Torriani played his first match as a starter. How do you rate his performance today?

“I think he did well in the first half. He had a difficult time with a pass, but Lorenzo doesn’t bear any responsibility for the team’s performance. In fact, in the first half he gave us time to try to make some changes in the second half. So Lorenzo just has to keep working. We have to improve as a team to be stronger.”

#1886. Barcelona and Spain defender Cubarsi wins Golden Boy award

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Barcelona and Spain centre-back Pau Cubarsi has been announced as the winner of the 2026 Golden Boy award.

The prize, which is handed to the best performer playing in European football under the age of 21, has now been won by four Barca players in the last six years.

Pedri, Gavi and Lamine Yamal collected the prize in 2021, 2022 and 2024, respectively, and it cannot be awarded twice to the same player.

Paris Saint-Germain's Desire Doue scooped the award in 2025, while Kylian Mbappe (2017), Erling Haaland (2020) and Jude Bellingham (2023) are among the other recent winners.

Cubarsi is the first defender to land the award since Matthijs de Light in 2018, after he helped Barca defend their LaLiga title and Spain win the World Cup for the second time.

𝗣𝗔𝗨 𝗖𝗨𝗕𝗔𝗥𝗦𝗜, 𝗚𝗢𝗟𝗗𝗘𝗡 𝗕𝗢𝗬 𝟮𝟬𝟮𝟲 https://t.co/y4LljnnhOg

— FC Barcelona (@FCBarcelona) November 9, 2026

The 19-year-old was also named the Young Player of the Tournament at the World Cup and finished 12th in the Ballon d'Or voting, as one of six Spain players to make the top 20.

Cubarsi led all players in the final for touches (139), successful passes (121), passing accuracy (96%), line-breaking passes (21) and clearances (six) in July's World Cup final, as La Roja beat Argentina 1-0 in extra time, thanks to Ferran Torres' goal.

There are only three instances on record (since 1966) of a player completing 100+ passes in a World Cup final. Cubarsi and his team-mate Rodri (101) are two of those, with Dunga the other, in Brazil's win over Italy in 1994 (130).

Cubarsi was one of two teenagers to start the showpiece match, alongside Yamal, as Spain became the first team to ever start multiple teenagers in a World Cup final.

Five players have now won the Golden Boy award while representing Barca, moving them further clear of Borussia Dortmund and Manchester United (three each) as the club with the most recipients.

Cubarsi has been named in Luis de la Fuente's latest squad, as Spain look to round off their Group A3 campaign with a perfect record, facing Czechia on Thursday and then England three days later.

#1885. Liverpool star handed surprise international call-up after injury lay-off

Liverpool’s Victor Munoz has been called up late by Spain.

The winger, who was part of La Roja’s World Cup-winning squad at last summer’s tournament, joined the Reds after the tournament in a £34.5million transfer from La Liga side Osasuna.

He has had a mixed start to life at Anfield, scoring two goals in his first 12 matches for the Merseyside club.

The forward, 23, made the switch to the Premier League side after an impressive single season with Osasuna, with eight goal contributions in 34 appearances in Spain’s top division.

Before that, he had come through Real Madrid’s youth system, and he made two apperances for the club’s first team in the 2024-25 campaign.

Now, he is a late call-up to Luis de la Fuente’s squad for the upcoming Nations League games, where Spain take on the Czech Republic and England, who they have a three-point advantage over at the top of Group A3.

For his country, Munoz has five senior caps and one goal, which he scored in a friendly against Serbia back in March this year.

He has struggled with a knee injury in recent weeks, missing three matches - the wins over Villarreal, Brighton and Chelsea across the Champions League, Premier League and Carabao Cup - before returning to action in the 1-0 home defeat by Arsenal at Anfield on November 1, as Kai Havertz netted the winner for the reigning Premier League champions.

#1884. Xabi Alonso takes aim at his Chelsea players after shock Sunderland defeat

Xabi Alonso was not looking for excuses after his Chelsea side was beaten 1-0 at Sunderland, admitting they did not defend or attack well enough.

The Black Cats were bottom of the Premier League table with just one win in nine games when they welcomed Chelsea to the Stadium of Light on Sunday afternoon.

The Blues returned to London with nothing, though, with an Enzo Le Fee penalty the difference between the sides.

There was controversy over the penalty decision, with Levi Colwill adjudged to have hauled down Brian Brobbey, although it looked like both players were pulling the shirt of the other.

Chelsea goalkeeper Mike Penders hit out at the decision, telling Sky Sports: ‘For me it wasn’t a penalty. He barely touched him, I think it was the other way round. He grabbed him.’

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Alonso was not singing from the same hymn sheet, telling the BBC: ‘I haven’t seen it back. Nothing to comment on the referee. It is something that is our fault. We could have done better.’

He added: ‘I think it’s an action where he can defend better. It’s our mistake.’

Alonso was impressed by Brobbey over the game, not just in winning the penalty, but felt his defenders could have done better against the big Dutchman.

‘From transitions out of almost nothing he got a couple of chances, he got the penalty as well,’ he said. ‘But we have been preparing for that, we have tried, we could have done better.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘He is not unstoppable. He is stoppable but when you defend better than we did today.’

Clearly the former Real Madrid boss did not like he saw from his defenders and he was also frustrated with what his forwards produced.

‘I think we didn’t deserve more than probably one point,’ he said. ‘Not much happened, to be honest. We didn’t produce enough to deserve to win.

‘We were against a low block we missed a bit of patience, a bit of quality, a bit of creativity on the last third to create more chances, you need to be more consistent to move the ball from one side to the other that we didn’t do good enough.’

It was suggested to Alonso that Sunderland’s physical superiority meant they could bully Chelsea, but the manager said: ‘Not bullied. There’s situations that we could have defended better. Situations that we could have had better advantages in attack.’

Defeat left Chelsea fifth in the table, while Sunderland climbed to 18th.

#1883. Sunday's Premier League results: Brilliant Brighton climb to second as Chelsea suffer shock Sunderland loss

By Ellis Stevens | 08 Nov 2026 16:08, Last updated: 08 Nov 2026 20:46

The Premier League's 10th matchday delivered another afternoon of exciting action on Sunday, with four fixtures taking place ahead of the final game between Manchester United and Aston Villa before the November international break.

Two of the division's so-called 'Bermuda Triangle' went head-to-head as Brighton & Hove Albion hosted Brentford, while the third member of the group, Bournemouth, travelled to face Ipswich Town.

Elsewhere, Premier League heavyweights Liverpool and Chelsea were also in action, facing up against Crystal Palace and Sunderland respectively.

Here, Sports Mole provides a roundup of Sunday's Premier League action.

"No goalkeeper is saving that!" Pascal Groß fires a penalty into the top corner to double Brighton's lead ? https://t.co/yARFiu19LL

Brighton & Hove Albion defeated fellow 'Bermuda Triangle' member Brentford 2-0 at the Amex Stadium, seeing the Seagulls climb to second in the Premier League standings.

Fabian Hurzeler's men have been one of the most impressive teams in the league this season, especially at home, where they remain unbeaten, and today's result marked their fourth win and fourth clean sheet in five home league fixtures.

Not only have Brighton's results impressed, but the Seagulls have had a knack for scoring screamers this season, and Diego Gomez added yet another wondergoal to his collection early in the match.

The midfielder sensationally picked out the top left corner with his weak foot just 15 minutes in, with Brighton boosted further by Igor Thiago's subsequent red card and Pascal Gross's emphatic finish from the spot.

Brighton continued to dominate and looked comfortable defensively, ultimately keeping their fourth home clean sheet and seventh of the season - just three less than they managed in the entirety of the 2025-26 Premier League campaign.

The victory lifts Hurzeler's side to second in the Premier League standings going into the November international break, while Brentford slide to eighth in the table after their second defeat of the term.

Enzo Le Fee dispatches the penalty as Sunderland take the lead against Chelsea! ?⚪️ https://t.co/cCtYsHVWB9

Sunderland secured a superb 1-0 victory against Chelsea at the Stadium of Light.

The Black Cats were the far more offensively dangerous side throughout the 90 minutes, but Enzo Le Fee's 36th-minute goal from the spot proved the only difference as Sunderland eventually claimed all three points.

Regis Le Bris' side, as a result, climbed away from the bottom of the Premier League table to 18th thanks to securing just their second win of the 2026-27 league season.

Chelsea, meanwhile, suffered their fourth defeat in the Premier League and dropped out of the Champions League places to fifth in the standings, with Xabi Alonso's side handed their second loss in the space of three league games.

Bradley Barcola and Florian Wirtz combine to put Liverpool 2-0 up! ? https://t.co/F6sw33FkYZ

Liverpool returned to winning ways with a 3-1 victory over Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park, ensuring Andoni Iraola's side avoided suffering a third straight defeat across all competitions.

The Reds have been winless inside 90 minutes in their last three matches, with a draw against Chelsea in the EFL Cup - which they did win on penalties - and losses to Arsenal and Fenerbahce in the Premier League and Champions League respectively.

However, Alexis Mac Allister's first-half header, Florian Wirtz's second-half strike and Alexander Isak's late finish sealed a streak-snapping victory for Liverpool, with Eddie Nketiah's late goal only a consolation for the Eagles, who were handed their seventh defeat of the Premier League campaign.

While Iraola's side now head into the international break in good spirits, as they climbed to fourth in the table after today's win, Pierre Sage goes into the November hiatus under increasing pressure.

The Crystal Palace boss has recorded just two wins and one draw in 10 league fixtures, with seven points after 10 games leaving the Eagles at the bottom of the standings.

What a start to the second half for Bournemouth! ? Ryan Christie's strike deflects off Leif Davis to double the Cherries' lead https://t.co/qSxUMe0wjD

Bournemouth defeated Ipswich Town 2-1 at Portman Road Stadium, extending their winning run to eight consecutive matches across all competitions.

Marco Rose, who won just two of his first eight matches at the helm, has overseen an incredible improvement over the past weeks, including leading the Cherries up to seventh after their fourth straight Premier League triumph.

The Cherries flew out from the blocks as Evanilson opened the scoring inside five minutes, meaning the striker has now scored in each of his last five Premier League appearances.

Ipswich were once again undone swiftly after kick-off in the second half, as Ryan Christie's effort deflected off Leif Davis and into the back of the net, doubling Bournemouth's lead.

However, the Jack Clarke pulled one back for the Tractor Boys from the penalty spot with 17 minutes to play, making for a nervy ending to the match, but the Cherries were able to cling onto the victory.

Bournemouth, as a result of the win, climbed to seventh in the table with 15 points, just three points outside the top four, while Ipswich remain 14th with 11 points.

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Sort of. The now-Inter Milan defender has made a comeback to north London as part of England’s Nations League camp for this month’s international break, after he was called up by Thomas Tuchel to be one of the Three Lions’ two left-back options alongside Lewis Hall of Newcastle United.

Spence, who starred at last summer’s World Cup in England’s run to the semi-finals in north America, starting in the 2-1 defeat by Argentina in Atlanta, Georgia.

Spurs had already signed Andy Robertson to add to their defensive numbers under Roberto De Zerbi, who oversaw a £380m summer overhaul of his first-team cohort.

Spence’s game time at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium already looked in jeopardy with Pedro Porro the club’s vice-captain and go-to option at right-back, while versatile midfielder Archie Gray as also deputised ably in that role.

At left-back, Destiny Udogie had established himself as the first-choice pick, despite his persistent injury issues.

Spence’s return to Hotspur Way, his former club’s training ground, was captured on social media, with the full-back taking to his Instagram story to post a photograph posing with three former team-mates.

They were two of Spurs’ injured players - Xavi Simons and Wilson Odobert - and Richarlison, who has been frozen out under De Zerbi after not being registered in the club’s Premier League squad this term.

The Brazilian failed to secure a departure out of the capital - unlike Spence - in the summer, and he has not featured for the club since the transfer window - and the squad registration deadline - slammed shut.

#1881. Michael Carrick responds to Man Utd relegation fears after Aston Villa draw

Michael Carrick downplayed fears Manchester United were in a relegation battle after a remarkable 4-4 draw with Aston Villa in the Premier League.

United will sit in the relegation zone of the Premier League during the November international break after a thrilling 4-4 draw with Villa at Old Trafford.

Aston Villa twice led by two goals but Manchester United produced two spirited fightbacks to avoid defeat and potentially prolong Carrick’s reign as manager.

Goals from Brazilian winger Alysson and Senegal striker Nicolas Jackson put Villa 2-0 up inside five minutes but the hosts were level by half-time thanks to Bruno Fernandes’ penalty and Youri Tielemans equaliser against his former club.

John McGinn restored Aston Villa’s lead just after half-time and the visitors appeared to have the game wrapped up when Leon Goretzka scored a fourth on 53 minutes.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

But injury-time goals from Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu saw Manchester United salvage a point and avoid a third successive league defeat.

The comeback rivalled the one United produced in the Champions League against Roma during the week but it remains to be seen whether it saves Carrick his job.

Despite avoiding defeat, the Red Devils slip to 18th in the Premier League after ten games, their lowest position at the stage of a campaign since 1986.

Carrick’s side have also gone eight league games without a win, matching a run they have endured just once before in the Premier League.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘I’m disappointed that we haven’t won the game,’ Carrick said. ‘We looked the better team for long parts of it and we’re making it difficult for ourselves with the goals that we’re giving away.

‘We’re not just giving away one, it’s two in succession that put us in such a difficult position. We did it the other night, we did it again today and have come back into the game and had a lot of the game, could have won it at the end.

‘So I’m disappointed we haven’t won the game. It’s just moments that we need to tighten up on. Individual moments where we’re giving teams goals that we don’t normally get.

‘If we tighten up that, there’s a lot of good in that performance. I thought we should have won the game. But conceding the goals we are is not helping us at all.

"That's not going to happen" 🗣️Michael Carrick responds to the notion that he could resign as Manchester United head coach 🔴 pic.twitter.com/q1fBKSXL7l

‘We have got to tighten up, it’s pretty obvious to say that. It’s giving us too much to do in games. But I thought we did a lot and feel that we should have won the game.’

Asked whether he feels Manchester United are in a relegation battle, Carrick added: ‘We’re in November. I don’t like this situation or the results but we can definitely do something about it.’

Responding to Carrick’s post-match interview, former Manchester United captain Roy Keane said: ‘It’s obviously difficult for the manager. He’s under pressure, no doubt

‘He talks a lot but doesn’t say much. I don’t know if that’s a tactic. Like a politician. He keeps saying we need to tighten up and there’s things we need to work on.

‘But they better get moving on that. It’s the worst start in how many years, all these stats aren’t very good. If you keep giving up goals and chances, it’s just going to continue.

‘What are we expecting to change over the next few weeks and months? What are they working on? They need to do a lot better than that.’

While Manchester United slipped into the relegation zone, Aston Villa stay 10th after extending their unbeaten league run to seven games.

‘The goalkeeper has to do better. It doesn’t help if your goalkeeper isn’t making saves, that hurts the team a lot.

#1878. Tottenham seek ban on journalist over anti-Spurs chants with Arsenal fans

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Tottenham have lodged a formal complaint to the Premier League about the actions of a reporter working for ESPN Brasil.

Joao Castelo-Branco, who works as an English football correspondent for ESPN, was seen in video footage shared on his personal social media taking part in anti-Tottenham chanting with Arsenal fans in Sao Paulo.

The video was shared on Castelo-Branco’s personal Instagram page as well as an account belonging to an ESPN podcast and has now led to Spurs filing an official complaint against the journalist.

As part of their complaint, Tottenham have asked the Premier League to prevent Castelo-Branco from covering the club in future. That includes attending matches, press conferences and potential interviews.

The exclusions would not affect any other reporter or the broadcaster themselves, with ESPN a Premier League rights holder in the Caribbean and South America.

Castelo-Branco apologised for his actions in an interview with The Times and said the videos had since been removed from both social media accounts.

“I wanted to apologise to the club for the video I recorded with Arsenal fans in Brazil singing a derogatory chant about Tottenham Hotspur,” Castelo-Branco said. “Given my role as a correspondent in the UK, I feel I made a mistake.

“The video was posted on the podcast Instagram page and reproduced on my personal page. I understand it can be offensive to Spurs and Spurs fans and I should have thought more about singing that and the reach it could have.

“ESPN was notified by the Premier League about Tottenham seeing and disliking the post, and we agreed to delete it. Hopefully we can move on, and I will rethink and be more careful with the boundaries of having that persona on the podcast.”

#1877. Stevenage vs Fulham Under-21s - prediction, team news, lineups

By Darren Plant | 08 Nov 2026 16:15

Stevenage and Fulham Under-21s square off on Tuesday night, with both teams already aware of whether they will feature in the EFL Trophy knockout stages.

While Stevenage sit top of Group B in the Southern section with successive wins and have secured their progress, the young Cottagers are already eliminated after back-to-back defeats.

Having failed with a surprise bid for promotion in 2025-26, Alex Revell will be disappointed that his Stevenage outfit are down in 16th position in the League One table.

However, a 2-2 draw at Leicester City in their last third tier outing was followed by an outstanding 1-0 triumph at Oxford United in the FA Cup first round.

Carl Piergianni's fourth-minute goal earned Revell's side one of the most notable victories of the weekend, and it keeps them interested in two different cup competitions for the foreseeable future.

In the EFL Trophy, Stevenage have already thrashed Walsall by a 6-1 scoreline and edged out Leicester by the odd goal in three on home territory.

Stevenage now have five wins and one draw from their last eight matches in all competitions, with a further notable success over Plymouth Argyle included in that run.

Meanwhile, Fulham Under-21s have conceded nine goals in their defeats to Leicester and Walsall.

The Foxes cruised to a 6-1 win when welcoming the young Cottagers to the King Power Stadium, before the Saddlers came through by a 3-2 scoreline.

Fulham Under-21s also suffered defeat to Worthing in the National League Cup on November 3, further highlighting their struggles against senior opposition.

On a more positive note, they did register a 4-1 win at Stoke City in their last Premier League 2 fixture, leaving them in fourth spot behind Southampton, Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea.

Fulham Under-21s form (all competitions):

Daniel Barden, Alfie Thornett, Terry Taylor, Matt Smith, Chem Campbell and Michael Mellon could all be drafted into the Stevenage XI.

Revell may also look to introduce at least one youngster into the starting lineup as he bids to rest as many senior players as possible.

Tommy Setford, Brian Broggio and Josh Magennis are all on international duty.

Barring any such selections, Fulham Under-21s may line up similar to the recent win over Stoke Under-21s.

In his first appearance of the season, Terrell Works scored a double, and the attacker should feature again after that 58-minute outing.

Barden; Vancooten, Casey, Thornett, Earley; Sanderson, Taylor, Smith, Campbell; Turhan, Mellon

Fulham Under-21s possible starting lineup:

Allen; Cooke, Gomins, Slade, White; Nwoko, Chingwaro; Zepa, Casey, Works, Sani

With Stevenage likely to rotate as much as regulations allow, Fulham may feel that there is an opportunity for a win. However, the young Cottagers already conceding nine goals leads up to predict a relatively comfortable victory for the home side.

#1875. Gary Neville names four players who will ‘get Man Utd relegated’ after Aston Villa draw

Gary Neville has slammed Manchester United’s failure to sign any new defenders last summer and says the back-four that finished the remarkable 4-4 draw with Aston Villa will ‘get the club relegated’.

The Premier League giants go into the November international break sitting 18th in the table after Villa twice blew two-goal leads to draw at Old Trafford.

United found themselves 2-0 down inside five minutes as Alysson and Nicolas Jackson took advantage of the hosts’ fragile defence.

Michael Carrick’s side were level at half-time thanks to Bruno Fernandes’ penalty and Youri Tielemans’ 44th-minute strike against the club he left last summer

Josh McGinn restored Aston Villa’s lead with a penalty straight after the interval and the visitors looked on course for a big win when Leon Goretzka scored a fourth.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

But Manchester United scored twice in injury-time – substitutes Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu with the goals – to salvage a point and avoid sitting joint-bottom during the international break.

Despite two comebacks, United’s current position is their lowest at this stage of a season since 1986, while their eight-game winless league run has only happened once before.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Manchester United finished the Aston Villa thriller with a back-four of Noussair Mazraoui, Leny Yoro, Ayden Heaven and Patrick Dorgu, and Neville said that line-up would struggle to avoid relegation to the Championship.

‘The reason Manchester United have conceded four goals is because they haven’t invested in the defence in the transfer window,’ he said on NBC Sports.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘Every one knew they had to do that, they needed defenders. The current ones are making mistake after mistake after mistake.

‘The defenders that finished that game will get you relegated. Watch the defensive errors… we all screamed in the transfer window that they have to bring some defenders in.

‘They had to bring the transfer budget forward and bring defenders in.’

Gary’s brother Phil, who also enjoyed incredible success at Manchester United as a player, added: ‘The back-four that finished the game – Mazraoui, Yoro, Heaven and Dorgu – that gets you relegated.

"Should be banging heads!" 😡Roy Keane discusses how Manchester United can improve their form pic.twitter.com/r7JZzj62LD

‘That back-four gets you the sack as a manager and that back-four cannot keep United, I don’t think, in the Premier League.

‘That back-four gets you relegated, it’s poor. It’s not good enough to play in the Premier League.’

Despite Manchester United’s grim position in the Premier League, Gary Neville doubts a change in the dugout would improve the situation in the long-term.

‘You can paper over the cracks and get a new manager bounce,’ he added. ‘When the new manager comes in, everybody’s happy for a couple of months and all of a sudden, six months later, it happens again.

‘You can keep changing the manager and thinking that’s going to be the answer. But this has been proven now over eight managers in 12 years, that’s not the answer.

‘Michael could leave, Michael might stay, we don’t know, the ownership don’t have a clue what to do.

‘It’s rinse and repeat. Amorim, Ten Hag, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, Carrick, Jose Mourinho, Louis van Gaal, David Moyes, Ralf Rangnick – some of them are world class managers who have had success, there are a lot of promising young managers there, ex players who know the club as well.

‘None of it has worked because if you recruit badly, if you’ve got poor performance department, poor recruitment department, you’ve not got leadership that is strong right through the spine of the football club you will fail.

‘Every organisation in the world will fail if you’ve not got an aligned leadership from top to bottom – your board and your ownership right the way through to the person who is stood on the pitch trying to play football.

‘There are real issues within that football club, you’ve got people doing those jobs who have never done those jobs before in senior positions.’

#1874. Manchester United: Why Patrick Dorgu equaliser vs Aston Villa stood as Old Trafford theory emerges

Manchester United benefited from home advantage regarding their controversial late equaliser against Aston Villa.

That is according to Sky Sports pundit Tim Sherwood, with the ex-Villa head coach claiming that the potential foul in the goal is never given ‘in the 96th minute at Old Trafford’.

Man United twice rallied back from two goals behind to record a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa, with their last two goals scored in second half injury time.

Goalkeeper Senne Lammens went up for a corner with United trailing, and while he did not get on the end of the cross, fans on social media believed he body-checked opposite number Zion Suzuki, preventing the Villa goalkeeper from claiming the ball.

Instead, substitute Patrick Dorgu sparked wild celebrations by heading home and levelling scores.

During Sky Sports’ Ref Watch segment, former Premier League referee Dermot Gallagher believed the decision to be correct.

Gallagher shared: “I think it is a goal - does he make a lot of contact? He does make contact, there is no doubt about that.

“Is Suzuki strong enough? I am not sure, we saw last week against Fulham a similar incident where he goes to punch the ball. He goes into an area that is congested and once he gets there, he needs to get a firm punch on it and he does not.

“There is minimal contact, although there is contact, there is no doubt about that. Lammens is not looking at the ball and that does go against him, but is he looking to find a space, so it is harder for the goalkeeper to come through?

“It is one where the referee makes the decision and we talk about VAR assisting the referee, it has to be about the referee, who says 'no' and I think the referee is right.”

But fellow pundit Sherwood was not in agreement, pointing out that Matheus Cunha also impacted Suzuki’s ability to play the ball.

Sherwood added: “I think it is a foul, but do you get it in the 96th minute at Old Trafford? No.

“Is Lammens looking at the ball? No. He is a goalkeeper and knows how much contact he needs to give Suzuki there.

“The main offender was Cunha, who grabs Suzuki's left arm, which is what stops him.”

Jay Bothroyd agreed with Sherwood, stating: “I do think Suzuki needs to be better, he needs to be stronger and get a punch away.

“Lammens clearly does not have his eyes on the ball, he is going into the 'keeper to put him off and there was some contact there when he went into him.

“If they had blown up for that, I would have known why. I think it is a foul as he is not looking at the ball and has gone into the 'keeper.”

#1873. Michael Carrick speaks out on Diogo Dalot future after Manchester United fans make feelings clear

Manchester United fans made their frustrations with Diogo Dalot very clear at Old Trafford on Sunday, but Michael Carrick has defended the under-fire full-back.

The bizarre match finished 4-4 with Aston Villa, as the visitors twice relinquished a two-goal lead to their struggling hosts.

Alysson and Nicolas Jackson had put the Villains 2-0 up within five minutes, only for Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans to put the Red Devils level by half-time.

Villa were two goals in front by 53 minutes as John McGinn and Leon Goretzka started the second half brilliantly and Old Trafford was stunned again.

However, Carrick’s men pulled off a remarkable escape in stoppage time as substitutes Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dourgu both scored after the 90-minute mark to rescue a point.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Dorgu replaced Dalot on 66 minutes after a nightmare performance from the Portugal international, which included conceding a penalty for felling Alysson, leading to McGinn’s goal from the spot.

When his number came up there were loud cheers from supporters at Old Trafford, which turned to boos as he left the field.

The 27-year-old has played in all 10 of Manchester United’s Premier League fixtures this season but when Carrick was asked if it was time for him to come out of the team, he pushed back and defended the full-back.

‘We’ve got to be careful with that, I think,’ said the Red Devils boss.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘I understand the frustration and the disappointment of the supporters. I get it, we’re all frustrated, we’re all disappointed. The players are as much as anyone, I guarantee you that.

‘Diogo gives absolutely everything. He’s played in different positions, he’s played really well at times.

‘He gives the penalty away today, he knows that. Maybe he can do a little bit better, alright, that’s part of it, he’s made a mistake.

‘He cares an awful lot and he’s giving everything. I like what he brings to the team, I like what he brings to the group, I like what he brings to the whole environment and the culture that we’ve got.

‘Picking a team and who plays the next game that’s a whole different decision and that’s a whole different game that we’ve got to look forward to now.’

Dalot signed for Manchester United in 2018 and has become something of a symbol of the mediocrity that fans have watched since then.

Gary Neville, who knows plenty about playing full-back for Manchester United, defended Dalot from criticism earlier this year, saying in January on his Sky Sports podcast: ‘He gets a really harsh view at times [from] quite a few United fans. I do think there’s a half-decent full-back in there, and I watch full-backs so closely.

‘I think he’s actually good in the air. I think he’s got good athleticism about him. I think he’s decent on the ball. I don’t think he’s a world-class full-back, but neither was I.’

He added: ‘I think he’s got something about him. I think he’s got 7/10 in him every single week, Dalot, but because we’ve seen him at left wing-back, we’ve seen him at right wing-back, we’ve seen him exposed so many times.

‘I think if he just played right full-back and played there all the time, I wouldn’t be getting rid of him in a hurry.

‘Now, other people might disagree with me, but I think I know the position of full-back, and I think he could do a decent job for Manchester United.’

Neville was not complimentary about the United defence on Sunday, though, saying on NBC Sports: ‘The reason that Manchester United have conceded four goals is they haven’t invested in the defence in the transfer window.

‘Everybody knew they had to invest in the defence. They needed defenders. They’re making mistake after mistake after mistake.’

The draw with Villa means Manchester United have won just one of their opening 10 games of the Premier League season and sit 18th in the table.

#1872. Arsenal boost after shock Noni Madueke snub as training plan revealed for new undroppable

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

When Thomas Tuchel named his latest England squad last week, the core that has been established at Arsenal was evident.

The Gunners had five players included for upcoming Nations League matches against Croatia and Spain. It is not just more than any other club, but more than the other five of the traditional ‘Big Six’ combined.

That is despite Bukayo Saka not being involved due to the quad injury he suffered against Bayern Munich last month.

Even with such strong representation, it was an Arsenal player not included in Tuchel’s squad who attracted the most attention.

Noni Madueke can feel incredibly hard done by to miss out on a return to the England setup.

He has stepped up significantly since the last international break and filled the void left by Saka in the Arsenal side as well as, or perhaps even better than, anyone could have expected.

The winger has three goals and an assist in his last nine appearances, eight of which have been starts. It is the best run of consistent minutes of his Arsenal career.

As unfortunate as he has been to not make the cut for England, Madueke’s exclusion should be to Arsenal’s benefit.

It is understood that Madueke will be flying abroad during this international break for some warm-weather training - something Mikel Arteta has happily signed off on.

The winger is viewing it as a period to build on his best run in an Arsenal shirt and he is determined to maintain the sharpness and intensity that has impressed Arteta in recent weeks.

The plan is for Madueke to then return to Arsenal’s training ground at London Colney towards the start of next week to begin preparations for Arsenal’s trip to Newcastle.

England XI vs Croatia: Confirmed team news and predicted lineup

Art After Dark is back with an exciting calendar of cultural events

It is a formula that has worked well for Madueke and Arteta is keen for it to be replicated.

The last international break, when the 24-year-old was also not called up by Tuchel, was something of a turning point for Madueke.

Up to that stage in the season, he had played just 23 minutes of Premier League football. Madueke was very much on the periphery of Arteta’s thinking.

One of the few first-team players not called up by their country, the extended three-week break offered Madueke the chance to switch off from football if he wanted to.

Instead, he flew to Portugal, not for a holiday but to train in the sun. Madueke asked for an individual training programme, determined to build his sharpness and prove a point to Arteta and Tuchel. He trained hard through the international break.

When Madueke then returned to Arsenal’s training ground, Arteta and his coaching staff were convinced they had a “different Noni” in front of them. Madueke’s commitment during that time in Portugal made a real impression on Arteta.

Even as the full squad gradually returned from international duty, it was still Madueke catching Arteta’s eye.

Arteta had been frustrated with Madueke earlier in the season, believing he was not doing enough to merit more opportunities.

He’s been incredible... he gave me no option but to select him

Mikel Arteta on Noni Madueke’s recent form

That stance changed over the last international break. Messages that were not being taken on board sufficiently earlier in the season were now getting the response Arteta demanded.

The sense from the Arsenal manager was that Madueke could not have done more to force his way into the team and he deserved to be rewarded.

In the first match back after that international break, Madueke started ahead of Eberechi Eze on the left wing against Leeds.

“He’s been the best player in the last 10 days,” Arteta said of Madueke’s training performances. “He gave me no option not to select him and not to play him today.”

Madueke was starting to make the left wing shirt his own but Saka’s injury necessitated a switch back to the right. He has played the full 90 minutes in every Premier League and Champions League match since then.

In a short space of time, Madueke has made himself undroppable. No player in the Premier League is creating more chances per 90 minutes this season. His figure of 3.57 is more than double what he produced last term.

Against Hull on Saturday, Madueke had more touches in the opposition box than any Arsenal player has managed in the league all season.

There is a relentlessness to the way Madueke attacks. He does not stop running at his man.

In the past, too much of that has felt chaotic, relying on high volume to cover for a lack of efficiency. Increasingly, Madueke is delivering the end product that has been the missing piece of his game.

Speaking after the Hull match, Arteta laid down the challenge to Madueke. Now he has had a “different Noni” at his disposal, Arteta wants even more.

“He’s been incredible,” the Arsenal manager said. “Now you are in that position, now you need to hold it and improve it, and he can still do that. So let’s see what he does in this break.”

#1871. Brighton 2-0 Brentford: Pascal Gross equals Mesut Ozil Premier League record

By Ben Knapton | 08 Nov 2026 16:16, Last updated: 08 Nov 2026 16:31

Brighton & Hove Albion playmaker Pascal Gross equalled a Premier League record set by Mesut Ozil in the Seagulls' 2-0 triumph over Brentford on Sunday afternoon.

Fabian Hurzeler's men enhanced their Premier League title credentials once again at the Amex Stadium, where first-half goals from Gross and Diego Gomez either side of Igor Thiago's red card did the damage.

After Gomez propelled Brighton into the ascendancy with just 15 minutes gone, Gross was given the chance to double the Seagulls' lead from the penalty spot thanks to Keane Lewis-Potter's challenge on Luka Vuskovic.

The veteran midfielder made no mistake with an incredible top-corner strike to rubber-stamp Brighton's victory, and in turn equal Ozil's record for the most combined Premier League goals and assists from a German player.

Gross has now had a direct hand 87 Premier League goals - 35 of his own and 52 assists - while Ozil managed 33 goals and 54 assists during his time in the top flight with Arsenal.

87 - Pascal Groß and Mesut Özil are now tied for the most goal involvements by ?? German players in the Premier League: Özil - 33 goals, 54 assists Groß - 35 goals, 52 assists Playmakers. https://t.co/hQxnGBczxO

The 35-year-old Gross has also had a direct hand in 10 goals in as many Premier League matches in the 2026-27 season, scoring four of his own while setting up six more for the Seagulls.

Already a fan favourite during his first stint at the Amex Stadium, Gross has been nothing short of a revelation for the Seagulls since returning from Borussia Dortmund in 2025 for a second stint on the South Coast.

Also now just one game away from reaching 300 in a Brighton kit, Gross will almost certainly break Ozil's record before the season is over, although he has a bit further to go to become the highest scoring German in Premier League history.

That record was broken just last week, as Arsenal's Kai Havertz scored his 46th Premier League goal against Liverpool, surpassing Ilkay Gundogan's previous best of 45 for Premier League Germans.

Nevertheless, Gross's 35 puts him third in the charts, while his next active closest challenger is Brentford's Kevin Schade, who has netted 24 goals in the English top flight.

Beating Arsenal at home, Manchester City away and slaying aside almost every other foe in their path, Brighton could do little more to cement their status as serious Premier League title challengers.

The Seagulls have now risen to second place in the Premier League table behind Arsenal, sitting five points adrift of the reigning champions and one clear of a struggling Manchester City side.

Furthermore, the Citizens' place in the top flight remains in major doubt as fans await the verdict of their appeal against 114 charges, while Liverpool and Chelsea have lacked consistency since the campaign began.

The sample size remains small, but after 10 matches, Brighton have shown every sign of lasting the course and pushing the holders all the way.

#1870. Michael Carrick told Man Utd star was ‘playing for himself’ in Aston Villa draw

Troy Deeney took aim at Amad Diallo following Manchester United’s 4-4 draw with Aston Villa, claiming the winger ‘flattered to deceive’ and appeared to be ‘playing for himself’.

United twice fought back from two goals down to come away from Old Trafford with a point in Sunday’s thriller at Old Trafford, but the result saw Michael Carrick’s men enter the international break in the relegation zone.

The hosts were punished for their sluggishness early on as Alysson and Nicolas Jackson made it 2-0 inside only four minutes, only for Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans to find the net and draw level.

The Red Devils were once again punished for a slow start, though, as John McGinn converted a 48th-minute penalty before Leon Goretzka capitalised on some calamitous defending from Leny Yoro to restore the visitors’ two-goal cushion.

Staring down the barrel of a fifth Premier League defeat, Carrick rang the changes in search of a route back into the contest in the second half – and it was two of United’s substitutes, Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu, who struck to salvage a draw at the death.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

But with his side hovering just one point above rock-bottom Crystal Palace, Carrick will know the scrutiny and speculation surrounding his future is likely to rumble on ahead of the club’s crunch match away to bitter rivals Liverpool in a fortnight’s time.

‘I spoke about this on our last episode on Thursday, I feel like we’re doing the same things with Manchester United,’ ex-Watford and Birmingham striker Deeney said of United’s latest performance on talkSPORT’s Premier League All Access Podcast.

There had been calls for Carrick to field Shea Lacey in place of Amad following the youngster’s outstanding cameo display in United’s midweek Champions League victory over Roma.

However, the United head coach stuck to his guns and kept faith with Amad, who would go on to have a tough afternoon at the Theatre of Dreams.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘Amad comes in and flatters to deceive,’ Deeney said of the Ivorian’s display.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

‘A lot of running into nothing, he was… today it felt like a lot of them were playing for themselves and going, “Look, I’m not the problem!”

‘Amad had about nine shots in the first half that were never going to be on target.’

On United’s problems in the centre of the park, Deeney continued: ‘I saw a midfield that was empty and vacated today.

‘Villa went through that midfield at will, many times in that first 75 minutes.’

Unai Emery made five substitutions before United’s late fightback, with goalscorers McGinn, Alysson, Goretzka and Jackson all removed, as well as the lively Johan Manzambi.

Asked whether the Villa manager had made a mistake with his changes, Deeney replied: ‘Absolutely.

‘I also thought it was one of the few times where he’d probably be very disappointed and would want to go back when you look at taking off Johan Manzambi, who I thought was excellent.

‘His ability to not only roll the player and keep the ball, but buy fouls and take them ten, 15, 20 yards up the pitch was excellent.

‘I think the game got too easy for Villa at 4-2 and I thought Emery started to think a little bit too far ahead, “Okay, I can rest these players”, obviously going away to international break.

‘Nicolas Jackson at times looked like Kylian Mbappe against that Manchester United team. He was dropping team, running in behind, he was 15 yards away from everyone.

‘But I just think he made too many mistakes and you can’t account for a goalkeeper having a shocker as well.’

Diogo Dalot appeared to be targeted with sarcastic cheers from the Old Trafford crowd when he was replaced for Dorgu midway through the second half.

Facing the media shortly after the final whistle, Carrick jumped to Dalot’s defence and encouraged supporters to get behind the players, especially when they are playing out of position.

‘Diogo, he gives absolutely everything,’ Carrick said.

‘He’s played in different positions, he’s played left-back, he’s played really well at times. He gives a penalty away today, that’s, you know, he knows that.

‘Maybe he can do a little bit better, all right, that’s part of it, he’s made a mistake, but he cares an awful lot and he’s giving everything.’

On Dalot, the United boss went on: ‘I like what he brings to the team, I like what he brings to the group, I like what he brings to the whole environment and the culture that we’ve got.

‘Picking a team and who plays the next game, that’s a whole different decision, but it’s a whole different game that we’ve got to look forward to now.’
