#1868. Chelsea sent new double penalty verdict as Morgan Rogers incident reviewed

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Three controversial moments during Chelsea’s 1-0 defeat by Sunderland at the weekend have been analysed by Sky Sports’ Ref Watch panel, with the Blues told why a penalty was given against them - and why they did not receive one themselves.

Every week former Premier League referee Dermot Gallagher is joined by pundits Tim Sherwood and Jay Bothroyd to analyse key decisions made across the top-flight during the previous weekend.

Sunderland defeated Chelsea at the Stadium of Light on Sunday thanks to an Enzo Le Fee penalty awarded in the first half.

Brian Brobbey was felled inside the area by Levi Colwill after the pair tangled, first pulling each other’s shirts outside of the box.

After they got into the area, Brobbey started to pull clear of his marker, only to go down.

Gallagher said of that incident: “They are both grabbing. It starts outside the area, the referee [Jarred Gillett] does not take sides, but once Brobbey gets in front of him and Colwill does not let go, that is when he falls foul of the penalty.

“Once he is in front, he is in the ascendancy and Colwill drags him to the ground, so I think penalty. He does clip his heels as well.”

Former players Sherwood and Bothroyd also both believed that Colwill tripped the Sunderland attacker.

Sherwood said: “They are both at it at first, then Brobbey grabs Colwill and puts him on his back like a rucksack and decides to wait for some contact on his legs. He obliges, he goes down and it is a penalty.”

Chelsea fans felt their side should have been awarded a penalty in the same half, with Cole Palmer challenged by Luke O’Nien right on the edge of the Sunderland box.

Discussing the incident involving Palmer, Gallagher believed that the referee identified Jules Ahoka as the offending player, rather than O’Nien.

Any contact from Ahoka would have been outside the box, but on closer inspection it was O’Nien’s boot that brought Palmer down - inside the area.

Arsenal sent clear new penalty verdict in call for law change

Chelsea injury update: Acheampong, Martinez and Joao Pedro latest return dates

Alonso disagrees with Chelsea player over controversial penalty decision

Discover a hidden island paradise in the Indian Ocean

No foul was given, and according to Gallagher, VAR could not overrule the on-field match official, unless there was serious foul play.

That was because Ahoka was deemed to have been the first offending player - even if no foul was given.

Gallagher explained: “The referee gives a foul against Ahoka. That is what he gives.

“O'Nien completes the action when he is in the box. Once he gives the first foul, that is it. What happens afterwards, he can only take action if he deems there is serious foul play.

“That is what he fed back. What he has to do is, when he is talking to VAR, he has to say who he thinks is the player [committing the foul].

“It is O'Nien's boot in the penalty area. The argument is that if he is on the line, it is a penalty. But it is O'Nien's boot; you can't see the ball.

“O'Nien goes second. VAR said Ahoka went first and he is the first offender. They didn't stop the game. The game went on.”

The game’s final flashpoint involved Chelsea star Morgan Rogers and Trai Hume. Rogers caught Hume in the head with his knee as he walked past the Sunderland defender, who was on the ground.

Gallagher said of that incident: "When you go on the wide camera, Rogers isn't looking at him. Maybe I'm giving him the benefit of the doubt, but only Morgan Rogers knows his intent. He may have accidentally done it, only he knows."

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Lamine Yamal will miss Spain's Nations League game against Czechia on Thursday due to a knee injury.

Yamal still played the full 90 minutes as Hansi Flick's side recovered from a goal down to move three points clear at the top of LaLiga, assisting the second of Fermin Lopez's goals and creating seven chances in total.

He became the first Blaugrana player to reach that figure in a LaLiga match against Atleti since October 2008, when Xavi did so under Pep Guardiola.

Yamal has had an outstanding start to the season, registering 25 goal involvements in 16 games across all competitions (13 goals, 12 assists) – the most of any player from Europe's top five leagues.

Michael Olise (61) and Pascal Gross (57) are the only players to create more chances than Yamal's 54, while he has also attempted (118) and completed (65) the most dribbles.

He is one of only two players to already reach double figures for goals and assists this campaign, alongside Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane (10 goals, 11 assists).

In a statement, the RFEF said Yamal, David Raya and Mikel Oyarzabal were expected to join their team-mates in training later this week, while Liverpool's Victor Munoz has been handed a late call-up to Luis de la Fuente's group.

#1866. Aston Villa chief points finger at Manchester United star after controversial incident

Aston Villa’s Director of Football Operations has hit out at the controversial decision to let Manchester United’s equaliser on Sunday stand.

A thrilling contest at Old Trafford finished 4-4 as the home side scored twice in stoppage time to rescue an unlikely point.

Villa went 2-0 ahead within five minutes thanks to goals from Alysson and Nicolas Jackson, before Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans leveled things up before the break.

The Red Devils started the second half as badly as they did the first as John McGinn scored from the penalty spot before Leon Goretzka made it 4-2 on 53 minutes.

As the clock ticked past 90 minutes it looked bleak for Michael Carrick, but substitutes Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu scored in injury time to give the home fans something to cheer.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Dorgu’s headed goal was not without controversy as Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki claimed he was impeded by his opposite number Senne Lammens who was up for the corner.

Manchester United legend Roy Keane did not think it was a foul by the Belgian, saying on Sky Sports: ‘I don’t think Suzuki gives himself the best chance of getting it, he’s underneath it, just take a step back and attack it. There are bodies in the way, but there’s lots going on, football is a contact sport. I have no problem with it.

"Football is a contact sport!" 🗣️Did Senne Lammens foul Zion Suzuki for Man United's equaliser? 🤔 pic.twitter.com/KCb1lHqPHP

‘A goalkeeper in this situation, he should take command of it. If he’s talking about getting blocked and pushed, why doesn’t he do that to the opposition players?

‘He’s got to come and be aggressive. When the ball comes in he’s on his heels. He’s got to be more aggressive and take command of that six-yard box.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

The incident will split opinion as Lammens seemed to look at Suzuki, turn his back to him and then purposefully nudge him with no attempt to play the ball.

That was certainly the stance of Damian Vidagany, who says referees had vowed to be harsher on such incidents.

Posting on X, Villa’s Director of Football Operations wrote: ‘To put in context this convenient narrative of “contact sport” we’ve been told by referees during the summer that this season to go to unbalance or push the GK on purpose on the six hard box was not going to be allowed anymore.

‘Lammens not even look at the ball, went straight to do a contact with the hip over Zion.

‘Having said that we played good match and we must do better than last 6 minutes. We will do and we will improve. But the rules are the rules and must be respected. That is a fact.’

Villa boss Unai Emery said his 24-year-old goalkeeper, who arrived from Parma over the summer, is still getting used to Premier League officiating, which is different to elsewhere.

‘When we are conceding the last goal in this corner, it is adaptation,’ he told Sky Sports. ‘Adaptation to the Premier League for Zion to settle here well. He must try to, because it is not the same timing. Here is not foul. They are pushing, they are disturbing the keeper.

‘Of course, in another countries, another leagues, they are not permitting it. Here, yes. We have to continue analysing, having experiences, and trying to avoid situation like we conceded.’

‘Are they sleepwalking into relegation? You’re 10 games in, one win. All competitions, 40 goals conceded,’ Keown said on talkSPORT.

Keown accepts that Manchester United showed some fight to respond at the death and also did so in their win over Roma earlier in the week, but thinks something is ‘very wrong’ with a team that continues to fall behind in matches.

‘Okay, I saw character and personality and saw it in midweek,’ said the former England defender. ‘But when you win a game like that against Roma, you have to put that in a bottle and channel all that energy from the first whistle against Villa and they were two goals down in each half within minutes.

‘Something is very wrong. The players are not motivated. You can’t keep coming back from the brink in the way that they did. Okay you’ll say that’s a bit of personality, but something is the wrong with the team and the way it defends.’

Carrick was not too down on his team’s performance overall, but insisted that it is just ‘moments’ that are costing Manchester United.

‘There was a lot happened in the game,’ he said. ‘It’s just the moments that are making it [difficult]. We’re kind of beating ourselves a little bit, with the moments that we’re giving away and goals that we’re giving away in tight clusters, that are making it a lot more difficult.

‘It’s hard enough anyway, but making it a lot more difficult than it should be. Football’s about moments. Football’s about what happens in both boxes in the end.

‘I think you take the moments that are totally avoidable, goals that we’re giving away, I actually thought we’ve played pretty well and were the better team for the most part, and I’m disappointed that we still haven’t won the game, to be truthful.

‘I thought we had most of the pressure. I thought we defended well, pressed well. We’re just giving them the moments that shape the game in some ways and then finished strongly and took something out of the game but still disappointing that we haven’t actually won it.’

He added: ‘It’s moments that are really causing us the problem. So if we can deal with that, a little bit of concentration, a little bit of confidence, a little bit of belief, a little bit of mentality, all that comes into making the right decisions

‘I’d say the last three games or so, there’s good things that give us a lot of encouragement that we can definitely win a lot of football matches with, and I feel like we should’ve won today even though we’ve still give too much away.’

#1863. Bristol Rovers vs Reading - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matthew Cooper | 08 Nov 2026 16:17

Bristol Rovers will be looking to cause an upset when they welcome Reading to the Memorial Stadium for an EFL Trophy clash on Tuesday.

The hosts have already been eliminated from the competition, while the visitors need a convincing victory to keep their hopes of reaching the knockout stages alive.

Bristol Rovers currently sit 17th in League Two with 16 points from their opening 14 matches, having made a difficult start to the campaign.

However, Steve Evans's side will take encouragement from their most recent outing which saw them beat Cambridge United 2-0 in the FA Cup.

Reiss Russell-Denny and Fabrizio Cavegn were on target for Bristol Rovers as they ended a run of seven games without a win across all competitions.

The Pirates have also struggled in the EFL Trophy, collecting just one point from their opening two group fixtures after losing to Chelsea Under-21s on penalties after a 2-2 draw and suffering a 4-1 defeat to Wycombe Wanderers.

Although they are already eliminated, Bristol Rovers will be keen to build on Saturday's FA Cup victory and build some momentum ahead of their return to league action.

Reading, meanwhile, are sixth in League One with 22 points from 14 matches and travel to Bristol following an emphatic 5-0 FA Cup victory over Peterborough United on Saturday.

Daniel Kyerewaa, Jack Marriott and Charlie Savage all found the back of the net before Jamie Reid came off the bench to bag a brace.

The Royals have also collected two points from their first two EFL Trophy fixtures, beating Wycombe on penalties after a 1-1 draw before suffering a 2-0 defeat against Chelsea Under-21s.

As a result, Leam Richardson's side need a sizeable victory to reach the knockouts as Chelsea Under-21s are three points above them and have a superior goal difference.

Bristol Rovers could keep faith with the side that beat Cambridge, with Cavegn set to lead the line alongside Joe Quigley.

Russell-Denny is expected to continue in midfield alongside Clinton Mola and Keenan Gough.

Reading may have to make at least one change after Udoka Godwin-Malife picked up a knock against Peterborough, with Ashqar Ahmed likely to replace him.

Marriott is also expected to be rested, having only just returned from injury, and Reid is likely to replace him after scoring his first goals for the Royals on Saturday.

Pereira; Ahmed, Knight, Masterson, Roberts; Fraser, Savage; Williams, Stokes, Kyerewaa; Reid

Greek international winger Christos Tzolis was signed from Club Brugge, but he has made only a limited impact thus far, in part down to injury.

#1860. Everton should not have been ‘written off’, claims Branthwaite

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Jarrad Branthwaite feels Everton were unfairly "written off" after their chaotic end to the transfer window.

Everton have won their last three games in all competitions, beating Newcastle United twice – in the EFL Cup and the Premier League – and Coventry City.

#1859. Tottenham: How major problem returned to bite Spurs as fears grow over only solution

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Tottenham had scored in all nine of their previous meetings with Leeds, but they could have no complaints about failing to find the back of the net at Elland Road on Saturday.

This was as timid an attacking performance as you are likely to see all season, and Spurs’ lack of cutting edge gave Leeds the encouragement they needed to push forward and break the deadlock with just over 10 minutes to play.

Roberto De Zerbi was scathing in his post-match assessment, criticising his players’ spirit, character and physicality as they let a fiery but evenly-contested affair slip away from them in the second half.

Tottenham weathered an early Leeds onslaught and began to piece together some fluid, attacking moves towards the end of the opening 45 minutes, but it was abundantly clear that something was missing.

Despite having 62 per cent of the ball, Spurs managed just seven shots in total, with a combined xG (expected goals) of 0.72. Leeds, by contrast, had 16 shots from just 38 per cent possession and generated an xG figure of 1.96.

In essence, Leeds should have scored more than once, while Tottenham would hardly have been deserving of an equaliser.

Results have seen an upturn over the last month, but Spurs’ inability to create consistent clear-cut chances from open play was an issue that was always likely to come back and bite them eventually.

In-swinging crosses from the left flank have been a productive route to goal this season, with Dominic Solanke (away at Manchester United) and Jan Paul van Hecke (at home to Crystal Palace) both scoring from such situations, but De Zerbi’s side are ultimately still too reliant on set-pieces to generate chances.

The fix for Spurs on paper is simple. The reality less so. They need James Maddison fit and ready to start.

Maddison is the only player in Spurs’ squad with the poise and precision to play between the lines and connect a functional midfield with a frenetic frontline.

Tottenham seek ban on reporter for anti-Spurs chants with Arsenal fans

Spence makes Spurs return after £25m transfer as reunion photo emerges

Tottenham told Bogle red card verdict after official complaint

Choose the right education path for your child

The problem is his availability. Maddison has started just twice this season and has not featured since coming off with a suspected groin issue during Spurs’ 2-0 victory away to Chelsea last month.

At the time, De Zerbi downplayed any fears of a serious injury, and he has since named him in the last two matchday squads.

Maddison is the only player in Spurs’ squad with the ability to connect a functional midfield with a frenetic frontline

However, in neglecting to bring him off the bench against both Palace and Leeds, there is growing concern that Spurs are back to square one with Maddison’s fitness.

The 29-year-old has been unable to train consistently in the last few weeks, and while fit enough to be made available for selection, De Zerbi clearly has reservations about his sharpness.

So much so that Dejan Kulusevski, who only recently returned after nearly a year-and-a-half out with a serious kneecap injury, has jumped ahead of him in the pecking order.

Kulusevski was one of three ineffectual changes De Zerbi made just past the hour mark against Leeds to try to wrestle back control. In reality, Tottenham needed Maddison’s ability to find space and dictate the tempo.

The international break has come at a good time for Spurs and Maddison, who will surely be targeting minutes at home to Ipswich in their first game back.

The longer they continue to struggle to create chances, though, the less patience there will be for Maddison and his patchy fitness record.

#1858. Steven Gerrard tells Chelsea to sign three players after Sunderland defeat

Steven Gerrard believes big-spending Chelsea still need to sign three ‘world-class’ defenders to compete for the Premier League title.

Chelsea’s inconsistent start to the season continued on Sunday as Xabi Alonso’s side were beaten 1-0 by Sunderland.

Enzo Le Fee broke the deadlock at the Stadium of Light with a first-half penalty after Levi Colwill was penalised for a foul on Brian Brobbey.

Chelsea had almost 70 per cent possession during the game but failed to create many clear-cut chances and returned to Stamford Bridge empty-handed.

A fourth defeat of the season leaves Chelsea fifth in the Premier League heading into the November international break, 11 points behind defending champions Arsenal.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

The Blues have conceded 16 goals in the league so far, the seventh-most in the division and more than any other team in the top-half of the table.

Asked whether Chelsea’s next round of recruitment needs to start with the defence, Gerrard said on The Overlap Daily, sponsored by Sky Bet: ‘100 per cent.

‘Chelsea have good defenders. I really like Reece James when he’s fit and available and he plays right-back. I think he’s the best right-back in the country.

‘I really like Colwill, because he gives them nice balance and the left foot. They’ve got a fantastic goalkeeper now, who I’ve worked with. And I look at the midfield and the front line and think, that can compete.

‘But with all due respect, I think for Chelsea to compete with your Arsenals, Man City’s, Liverpool’s, and the top end of the Champions League, I think they need to find world-class centre-backs and a world-class left-back.

‘Now, that’s a back four that can compete and proved that it can compete at the top end of the Premier League and the top end of the Champions League.

#1857. Mansfield Town vs Chesterfield - prediction, team news, lineups

By Darren Plant | 08 Nov 2026 16:30

Mansfield Town play host to Chesterfield on Tuesday evening having already been eliminated from the EFL Trophy.

However, the visitors to Field Mill have booked their place in the knockout stages with five points from their opening two games in Group D of the Northern Section.

Nigel Clough will be disappointed with how Mansfield have fared in the EFL Trophy, losing to Manchester City Under-21s and Port Vale respectively.

Six goals have been conceded in those contests, including four versus City, but Clough will be more encouraged with their form in League One and the FA Cup.

At the weekend, Mansfield recorded a 3-0 victory over National League North high-flyers Macclesfield FC, avoiding what was viewed as a genuine cup upset possibility.

They had previously failed to beat or score versus Notts County and Wigan Athletic, yet 11 points have been accumulated from their last six matches in the third tier of English football.

That run has kept the Stags in 11th position in the League One table, just seven points adrift of second place.

In sharp contrast to Mansfield in this competition, Chesterfield have racked up five points, as well as scoring five goals versus Man City.

Paul Cook's team followed that with a penalty-shootout success over Port Vale after a 1-1 draw, and a top-two spot is now assured.

Nevertheless, Cook will have concerns over Chesterfield's recent inconsistency, with there being 18 goals in their most recent three encounters.

Although a 4-1 loss at Newport County was posted on October 30, the Spireites registered a 5-1 triumph over Crewe Alexandra in the preceding game and edged out Yeovil Town by a 4-3 scoreline in Saturday's FA Cup tie.

Clough could draft Harry Lewis, Owen Dodgson, Elliott Hewitt, Kyle Knoyle, Luke Bolton, Ollie Taylor and Tyler Roberts into his Mansfield starting lineup.

The formation that Clough will use is not obvious, a consequence of deploying different tactics for the previous two EFL Trophy games.

Deji Oshilaja is expected to remain sidelined through injury.

Meanwhile, Chesterfield youngsters Victor Huart, Gunner Elliott and Jaylen Zarb have all been called up for international duty.

Saliba is closing in on a long-awaited return from injury, having featured in Arsenal’s matchday squad for their Champions League clash against Slavia Prague last week.

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

David Raya has been named in the FIFPRO World 11 for 2026, weeks after missing out at the Ballon d’Or.

The team is voted for by 19,806 professional men’s footballers worldwide and this year’s lineup has now been announced.

Raya got the nod in goal and in doing so becomes only the second Arsenal player to make the FIFPRO World 11 since it launched in 2005.

Thierry Henry was named in the side in 2006, alongside Ronaldinho and Samuel Eto’o as the forwards, and Raya has now joined the Arsenal legend in an extremely exclusive club.

“Thank you guys for voting me in the FIFPRO World 11,” Raya said.

It comes after Raya was pipped to the Yashin Trophy last month.

The award for the best men’s goalkeeper instead went to Raya’s Spanish team-mate Unai Simon, who started every match in the World Cup-winning campaign.

Raya came second in the voting, the best finish of his career, but he missed out picking up the award at the Ballon d’Or ceremony.

However, he has now been recognised for a year in which he won the Premier League with Arsenal and played a key role in Mikel Arteta’s side making it to the final of the Champions League as well.

Raya was one of only two Premier League players to be named in the FIFPRO World 11 this year, along with Erling Haaland.

Harry Kane did not make the cut, despite winning the Ballon d’Or. Haaland, Lionel Messi, Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal were instead chosen as the forwards.

#1854. Paul Scholes blasts Man Utd players for ’embarrassing’ moment after Aston Villa draw

Paul Scholes has urged Manchester United’s struggling players to ditch ’embarrassing’ laps of honour after games.

The Red Devils are sitting 18th in the Premier League going into the November international break after winning just one of their ten games so far this season.

The last time United were in such a low position at this stage of the season was in 1986, while their record of eight league games without a win has only happened once before in the club’s history.

Michael Carrick and the Manchester United squad walked around the pitch applauding the fans following a humbling 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth at Old Trafford at the end of last month.

Carrick was serenaded by the United fans despite the club’s dismal position but the supportive chants soon turned to boos directed at the players once the ex-England midfielder made his way down the tunnel.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

The squad performed a similar lap of appreciation after Sunday’s thrilling 4-4 draw with Aston Villa but Manchester United legend Scholes was less than impressed by the gesture.

‘I tell you one thing they need to do, stop doing these laps of honour after every game,’ Scholes said on The Good, The Bad & The Football podcast.

‘What the f**k. It’s so bad. Jesus, it’s embarrassing. Every game’s like the last game of the season. Just get off!’

Fellow former Manchester United midfielder Nicky Butt added: ‘That’s pissing me off as well. A lap of honour after a draw…’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

United twice trailed by two goals against Aston Villa but produced a spirited comeback to avoid a fifth defeat in ten Premier League games.

Gary Neville praised the ‘persistence’ of Carrick’s side but was also critical of the post-match scenes, claiming the players are ‘almost causing themselves emotional damage’.

‘You have got to admire their persistence, they kept going,’ Neville told NBC Sports. ‘The defensive errors were shocking and we’ll discuss that shortly.

‘But this lap around the pitch… I played for Manchester United 602 times and I always appreciated the fans at the end of the game.

‘But this pattern of them walking around the pitch after defeats by Bournemouth and a 4-4 at home against Aston Villa, it’s almost painful to watch. They’re almost causing themselves emotional damage.

‘This just can’t go on, can it? It’s absolutely desperate. Michael will be proud of them and the fans are singing his name because they love him but this is a really sorry situation.’

The hierarchy at Old Trafford are currently reviewing Carrick’s position and weighing up whether to make a change during the international break.

Eddie Howe, Julian Nagelsmann and Antonio Conte have all been linked with the job, although Manchester United could yet show more faith in Carrick.

The Red Devils, sitting just one point above bottom place in the Premier League, return to action with a daunting trip to Anfield to face arch-rivals Liverpool.

#1853. Tottenham get major new Mathys Tel injury update as statement issued after squad announcement

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Tottenham forward Mathys Tel has been forced to pull out of France’s Under-21 squad.

The decision comes after Tel had to eventually be substituted due to being on the receiving end of Jayden Bogle’s strong tackle during the 1-0 loss to Leeds at Elland Road on Saturday.

Replays showed the the Leeds defender had landed his studs on Tel’s left Achilles, though he avoided any punishment from referee John Brooks.

In addition, while the Video Assistant Referee (VAR) reviewed the challenge for around four minutes, they ultimately deemed it did not meet the threshold for serious foul play.

Tel, however, departed Elland Road with his left foot in a protective boot and Spurs head coach Roberto De Zerbi was fearing the worst.

“Bad injury, and now we have to make the medical check,” De Zerbi said in his post-match press conference.

“In the next days we will know what is the problem.”

As confirmed by French Football Federation (FFF) on Monday, Tel will not be linking up with the France U21s as a result of the injury, meaning he will miss matches against Italy and England.

A statement reads: “Having suffered an injury with his club Tottenham, Mathys Tel is forced to withdraw from the France Under-21 team training camp which began this Monday at the CNF Clairefontaine.”

It still remains to be seen how long Tel will be sidelined for, with a further update likely to follow during the international break or when De Zerbi addresses the media in the pre-Ipswich press conference later in the month.

Standard Sport understands Spurs are set to submit a formal complaint about the decision to not send off Bogle, writing to refereeing body, Pro Ref, for an explanation.

#1852. Man United break another unwanted record vs. Aston Villa after Alysson, Nicolas Jackson goals

By Ben Knapton | 08 Nov 2026 16:50, Last updated: 08 Nov 2026 17:00

Manchester United have broken yet another unwanted club record after falling 2-0 down inside just four minutes against Aston Villa.

On the back of Tuesday's extraordinary 3-2 win over Roma in the Champions League, Michael Carrick could have been forgiven for expecting a fierce response domestically on Sunday afternoon.

However, the Englishman instead oversaw yet another disastrous opening, as Villa winger Alysson took just one minute to break the deadlock with a low strike through Senne Lammens's legs.

The Red Devils then found themselves two goals behind just a few moments later, as Nicolas Jackson followed in after a Lammens save to tap home the visitors' second.

Jackson's strike marked a shocking new low for Man United, who broke their record for the quickest time to fall 2-0 down in a Premier League game at three minutes and 40 seconds.

2 - After three minutes and 40 seconds, this is the earliest Manchester United have ever been 2-0 down in a Premier League game. Slumber. https://t.co/76iMwVLhTK

Boos rang out around an already febrile Old Trafford following Jackson's goal, the ground already awash with a sea of green and yellow in protest against the Glazer family's ownership of the club.

Carrick and United's players were subsequently subjected to a collection of brutal chants from the crowd, such as "you're not fit to wear the shirt" and "you're getting sacked in the morning".

Villa fans also took aim at former midfielder Youri Tielemans, chanting "you used to play for a big club" and poking fun at Bruno Fernandes's recent public criticism, bellowing out "Bruno's right, you're f****** s****".

However, Fernandes then gave Man United a sliver of hope from the penalty spot, calmly sending Zion Suzuki the wrong way after Matheus Cunha was scythed down by Boubacar Kamara.

If the Red Devils cannot fight back to beat Villa, though, they will enter the international break in 19th place in the Premier League table after Sunderland's surprise 1-0 win over Chelsea lifted the Black Cats off the bottom.

Even if Man United fell to a catastrophic loss vs. Roma in midweek, Carrick would have almost certainly taken the reins against Aston Villa, as the hierarchy always intended to get to the international break before conducting a thorough review.

The former Red Devils midfielder is still widely adored by the majority of the fanbase, whose frustrations are instead directed towards the Glazers, INEOS and the players themselves.

Man United cannot correct years of terrible transfer calls and a toxic culture overnight, but they can make a coaching change in the blink of an eye, and Carrick would undoubtedly be the fall guy if the powers-that-be decide that change if necessary.

Fernandes publicly calling out the tactics of the coaching staff hinted at discontent behind the scenes, and unless Man United pull off another fabulous fightback on Sunday, Carrick will surely be taking charge of his beloved club for the final time.

#1851. Premier League verdict may be impacting Man City results, says Neville

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Manchester City's guilty Premier League verdict is a "cloud" hanging over the club that may be impacting their recent performances, Gary Neville has hypothesised.

In late September, the Premier League confirmed City had been found guilty of all charges related to "serious breaches" of the competition's financial rules over a nine-year period between 2009 and 2018.

City were also found guilty of the majority of charges relating to the club's failure to comply with the Premier League's investigation.

While City have pledged to fight that verdict, rumours have swirled regarding the possible punishments that could be handed down, with pundits and supporters suggesting huge points deductions, automatic relegations or the stripping of past titles.

Initially, Enzo Maresca's squad did not appear to be affected by the off-pitch noise, as City won seven straight Premier League games to start the campaign.

However, they have since succumbed to defeats against Aston Villa (2-1), Brighton (1-0) and Nottingham Forest (3-1).

They are just the second team in English top-flight history – after Sheffield Wednesday in 1904-05 – to win their first seven games of a season before losing their next three.

And former Manchester United defender Neville has now questioned whether City's players are starting to be impacted by the speculation.

"Something's just not right at the moment and it's worrying. Things point towards the obvious cloud hanging over the club," Neville told NBC Sports' Premier League Mornings.

"Is it finally catching up with them, in terms of the mental fatigue of the negative publicity they've had, and the effect it's had on the players?

"Are they drained physically and mentally through that, or are they just going through a bad patch?

"Either way, Maresca has got to sort it out quite quickly in the international break, because that won't be tolerated. Losing games like that doesn't happen very often."

Club statement.  https://t.co/yrJ8Z0A52Y https://t.co/0NP2k33JT9

— Manchester City (@ManCity) September 29, 2026

And Neville says speculation over City being thrown out of the Premier League – and the knock-on effect such a punishment would have on their players – is bound to be a distraction.

He added: "Those players will constantly be getting asked, 'What do you think is going to happen? What happens if they do get relegated? Will you stay?'

"Now you imagine your family is having to put up with that, your agent's thinking about those things… it can't be ruled out as a factor that's going to start to seep in.

"If you lose a football match or two, you can start to look at that as an excuse, but they've got to play better, they've got to compete in games, they've got to make sure that they do better on the pitch from a tactical and physical perspective.

"But I do believe it will be having some impact, just because of the weight of what's been hitting them, from a publicity point of view."

City will spend the international break third in the Premier League, six points adrift of Arsenal and one behind Brighton, with Fulham being their next opponents on November 21.

#1848. Dowman weaves his magic and new signing shines as Arsenal hit ground running

Teenage sensation Max Dowman was the star of Arsenal’s first pre-season match, as he scored one goal and assisted another in a 4-1 victory over Girona.

Dowman, 16, was joined on the scoresheet by new signing Christos Tzolis, who struck with a low effort in his first game since his £34m move from Belgian side Club Brugge.

Established attackers Kai Havertz and Gabriel Jesus also scored for the Premier League champions, who were largely comfortable against opposition from the Spanish second tier.

Here are four things Telegraph Sport learnt from the match:

It was this time last year that Dowman first announced his remarkable talent to the wider world. Then only 15, he sparkled in pre-season and made it clear to Mikel Arteta that he was ready to impact matches at the highest level.

A year on, Dowman is now an established first-team player. He is the youngest ever Premier League winner and the competition’s youngest ever scorer, and he looks set to make even more of a mark this season.

In this friendly against Girona, Dowman created Arsenal’s opening goal with a gorgeous defence-splitting pass for Havertz. He did so after receiving the ball under pressure and spinning into space. Dowman then scored Arsenal’s third with a powerful low drive from the edge of the box.

Dowman is in competition with Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke for a place on the right wing, which means this summer represents a huge opportunity for the teenager. After playing for England at the World Cup, Saka and Madueke will both miss most of pre-season.

Dowman, therefore, has a serious chance of going into the new campaign as the starting right-winger. The Community Shield on August 16 must be a target in his mind.

“We know what he’s capable of doing,” Arteta said. “We want to be more consistent in terms of the performances and the actions that he can deliver, but I think today he had a really good game.”

Arsenal are close to completing a deal for Newcastle United captain Bruno Guimarães but, for now, their only outfield signing of the summer has been Tzolis. This was the Greek winger’s first match in front of supporters and he immediately demonstrated why Arsenal were willing to pay £34m to buy him from Club Brugge.

With Tzolis, it is all about the final product. Goals and assists. He struck 22 times for Club Brugge last season, and registered 29 assists.

How did he produce such impressive numbers? The answer could be seen in his first-half goal against Girona. Receiving the ball on the left wing, Tzolis quickly accelerated towards the penalty area and unleashed a low shot. It was perhaps a more direct approach than Arsenal would usually have seen from Leandro Trossard, the player Tzolis has replaced, and it caught Girona off-guard as the ball deflected into the net.

“I’m very pleased with him,” Arteta said. “First of all, the way he has adapted to the club, to the team. The connection he’s already generating with the boys. I think you’re going to love the player.

“A player who’s very direct. He’s got the goal between the eyes. He has a lot of similarities with Leo [Trossard] in a lot of the things that he can do and the spaces he can occupy. And then the work rate that he has... He’s a boy that comes with so much hunger. He wants to prove himself, it’s a dream for him. And we are here to help him.”

Havertz was one of the few Arsenal players who benefited from playing at the World Cup. His injury issues mean that, unlike most of his team-mates, he did not end the 2025-26 season in a state of exhaustion.

After returning to the pitch in the spring, Havertz enjoyed an impressive end to the campaign for Arsenal. He then performed well at the World Cup, scoring three goals for Germany.

He remains one of Arteta’s favourite players, not least because of his versatility. He started in attack in the crucial end-of-season games in May, but played in midfield against Girona. His low finish, from Dowman’s pass, represented his eighth goal in his last 12 matches for club and country.

Girona’s goal, scored by Arnau Martínez, was perhaps the only alarming moment of this comfortable pre-season victory. Martínez was unmarked from a left-wing corner when he powered a header into Arsenal’s net.

For a group of players who pride themselves on their set-piece prowess, this was a disappointing moment. It also perhaps showed Arsenal’s reliance on their two first-choice centre-backs, William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhães, when they are defending crosses into their box.

Gabriel arrived at Arsenal’s pre-season training camp a few days ago, so he should be in good shape by the start of the new campaign. Saliba, though, will be missing for months with a back problem.

Without Saliba’s height and power, will Arsenal be as effective from set-pieces in the opening chunk of the campaign? Coventry City, Arsenal’s opponents on the first night of the season, will undoubtedly look to test the champions in these situations.

The reigning Premier League champions are handed the Costa Brava Trophy, which is half-heartedly lifted into the air by White. There will be far bigger trophies on offer to Arsenal in the upcoming campaign.

Arsenal have cruised to a routine 4-1 win over Girona, with Havertz, Tzolis, Dowman and Gabriel Jesus all finding the net. Arteta will be delighted with his side’s professionalism and ruthlessness.

Meslier takes too long on his goal kick, gifting a corner to Girona. However, the delivery from the hosts is so poor as it flies harmlessly out of play. That sums up Girona’s difficult evening.

There is another round of substitutions for both sides.

Two more changes in the offing...↩️ Jesus, Copley🔛 Agustien, Julienne🔴 1-4 🔵 (85) pic.twitter.com/3qt6N63qzq

🔁 Últim canvi al Girona:➡️ Stuani⬅️ Pyshchur

Once again, Meslier makes a pivotal stop on his Arsenal debut. Martin clips an exquisite pass over Arsenal’s defence to the onrushing Ruiz, who is through on goal. The striker takes the chance first time, but Meslier is there to make another crucial save.

Arsenal’s makeshift line-up, which is full of Hale End graduates, is holding firm, with Girona evidently struggling for attacking inspiration. If Arsenal can see out this victory without any injuries, then it would have panned out exactly how Arteta would have wanted.

Girona carelessly give possession away in defence, allowing Nelson to dribble towards the penalty area. The winger floats a cross into the box, which is met by O’Neill, but the forward’s lofted header hits the top of the bar.

There is cooling break in this second half to give both sets of players a quick breather. It’s been a professional performance from Arsenal, who now have various academy prospects on the pitch. Can any of them follow in Dowman’s footsteps and make an eye-catching impression in this match?

Girona make another flurry of changes, giving the youngsters from the club’s academy an opportunity to impress.

🔁 Més canvis al Girona:➡️ Gibert, Holmes, Izan, Misehouy i Jastin⬅️ Arnau, Fran Beltrán, Francés, Bryan i Minsu pic.twitter.com/fb7aVKloFx

Kabia gets to the byline and intelligently pulls a cross back to Gabriel Jesus, who curls a first-time strike narrowly wide of the far post as Arsenal search for a fifth goal.

Meslier showcases his magnificent reflexes, making a world class save to deny the recently-introduced Ruiz from close-range after he latched onto Martinez’s dangerous delivery.

Both sides make numerous changes to their line-ups to manage minutes and give the younger players some game time.

A flurry of substitutions...↩️ Arrizabalaga, White, Tzolis, Nwaneri, Dowman, Vieira, Mosquera, Calafiori, Lewis-Skelly🔛 Meslier, Nelson, Kabia, Ibrahim, Copley, Clarke, O'Neill, Harriman-Annous, Ogunnaike🔴 1-4 🔵 (61) pic.twitter.com/GDXL0JRzkT

🔁 Canvis al Girona:➡️ Krapyvtsov, Antal, Badia, Iván Martín, Abel i Pyshchur⬅️ Gazzaniga, David López, Van de Beek, Lass, Àlex Moreno i Vanat pic.twitter.com/3T6Pb9d9fG

Dowman was the breakout star of pre-season last year, when he was only 15, and he has started this campaign in similarly thrilling fashion. One assist, one goal. As you would expect, he looks bigger and stronger.

Arsenal overturn the ball in midfield and it breaks perfectly into the Brazilian’s path. Gabriel Jesus is one-on-one and makes no mistake, applying a devastating finish to make it 4-1 and put the result beyond any doubt.

The 16-year-old prodigy now has a goal and an assist. Dowman picks up the ball in the right attacking pocket, palms off Moreno, who bizarrely throws himself to the ground holding his face, before firing a resounding effort into the bottom corner. He’s such a talented footballer and looks at home in Arsenal’s first team.

Out of nothing, Girona have pulled a goal back. Kim whips a corner into the box, with the unmarked Martinez slamming a magnificent header into the top corner, leaving Kepa rooted to the spot. Arteta will be furious with his side’s complacency there.

🎯 El gol d'Arnau pic.twitter.com/Op6oX3LBzK

The team known as “Set Piece FC” looked alarmingly vulnerable at that Girona corner. Perhaps this is simply the reality of life without William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhaes. The good news for Arsenal is that Gabriel is back with the squad and should be ready to go for the start of the campaign. The bad news is that Saliba’s back injury will rule him out for months. Will that lead to more sustained vulnerability over the opening chunk of the season?

Girona have sent a host of players out to warm up. They’re playing in their fourth pre-season match, with their league campaign due to start on August 16 against Leganes.

We are back under way for the second half.

That was a straightforward half for Arsenal. Arteta will be pleased with Havertz’s showing in his 33 minutes on the pitch. After missing so much of last season through injury, it has been a good summer for Havertz so far. He scored three goals in Arsenal’s final six games of 2025/26, and then netted four times for Germany in June.

The 2009-born playmaker was Arsenal’s standout player in that first half. Dowman’s confidence and class on the ball has been brilliant, with his expertly-crafted assist for Havertz’s opener an obvious highlight.

Arsenal are in complete control here in Spain thanks to first-half strikes from Havertz and Tzolis.

A dominant first-half display in Girona 🙌 pic.twitter.com/ZprG2xLYyj

Dowman dribbles into the penalty area with ease, drifting past a couple of defenders before he is apprehended by Moreno. He goes down, but there is very little in the challenge.

Arsenal are in cruise control here. Girona are chasing shadows. Unsurprisingly, there’s a real gulf in class and quality between the two sides.

Once again, Dowman dances away from Moreno. The youngster sets up White with a reverse pass, but the Arsenal captain’s disappointing cross drifts out for a goal kick.

Tzolis registered 22 goals and 29 assists for Club Brugge last season. He is an end-product machine, and that goal was a little indication of how he racks up such eye-watering numbers. After receiving possession on the left wing, he was so quick to shift the ball onto his right foot and fire the shot at goal. He describes himself as a “direct” player and that was evidence of it.

There are three early changes for Arsenal, with Gyokeres, Havertz and Hincapie taken off for Gabriel Jesus, Vieira and Salmon.

We're making a triple substitution...↩️ Havertz, Hincapie, Gyokeres🔛 Vieira, Salmon, Jesus🔴 0-2 🔵 (32) pic.twitter.com/NtpnUsfAY6

The new winger is one-on-one with Martinez and darts inside, before firing a low effort into the bottom corner. It took a slight deflection, leaving Gazzaniga with no chance. Tzolis has looked lively and slotted into Arsenal’s attack seamlessly so far.

Tzolis is slipped into the penalty area from his left-wing berth, but instead of shooting, he tries to find Gyokeres with a pass. Girona surround the Swede before Dowman’s follow-up strike is blocked.

Since their goal, Arsenal have assumed real authority of this encounter and look like the far superior side.

Girona captain Martinez slams a powerful long-range effort at goal, but it fizzes wide of the bottom corner. Kepa seemed to have it covered regardless.

Arsenal are hunting for a second, with Lewis-Skelly picking out Havertz with a floated pass. The former Chelsea man is inches away from teeing up Gyokeres for a second, but Gazzaniga is there to make a goal-saving interception. Dowman has also been heavily involved in these early stages, providing the assist for Havertz’s opener.

After his extraordinary breakthrough campaign last year, Max Dowman has a huge opportunity this summer. With England wingers Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke not returning until later in pre-season, Dowman has a chance to take ownership of the right wing position ahead of the Community Shield. His assist for Kai Havertz, a lovely measured pass after an excellent piece of skill in midfield, was a sign that Dowman means business.

Dowman drifts inside and pops up in the right channel, wriggling past Moreno, before threading a delightful pass through to Havertz. One-on-one, the German calmly slots a close-range effort into the bottom corner, giving Arsenal a well-deserved lead. So much credit must go to Dowman, who has started this game excellently.

Girona have some sustained possession to take the sting out of the game then burst into Arsenal’s penalty area, with the ball attempted to be pulled back to Van De Beek. The visitors have good numbers defending and comfortably deal with the danger.

Tzolis floats a free kick into the box, which Gyokeres meets at the back post. The striker directs the ball back across goal towards Calafiori, whose close-range header is caught by Gazzaniga.

It also appears that Havertz and Nwaneri have been tasked with quite free-roaming attacking midfield roles, with Lewis-Skelly positioned as a one-man holding pivot. It’s a strong but experimental line-up from Arteta.

After suffering an injury at the end of last season and missing the World Cup, White returns to action here this evening and wears the armband. He will look to support Dowman, who appears to be starting on the right wing.

It’s been a confident start from Arsenal, who are stroking the ball around in a very assured manner. Havertz looks to pull the strings by firing a low cross towards Gyokeres, but the delivery is scrambled clear by the Girona backline.

White leads Arsenal out onto the pitch to face Girona, who boast the likes of Van de Beek, Gil and Moreno in their starting XI.

Talking earlier this week, Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta sent out a determined message to other clubs by outlining their ambitious transfer plans.

“A lot is happening,” Arteta said. “We all know about the context of this transfer window. From ownership to the board, the sporting director and myself, we know that we want to take this club to a different level.

“That is going to require a better squad, better individuals. We have identified where we have opportunities to grow and to improve and to evolve our game and what is going to be needed to achieve that. Hopefully very soon we can start to put things in a very concrete way.”

Arteta also believes that last season’s Premier League title has served as added motivation for his squad to improve and hit new heights.

“This has to be the start and this has to be the standard,” he said. “Excellence has to be our standard and this has to drive to attack the future. The way we behave daily with more and more determination and ambition, because we’ve shown that we’ve got it. Now we have to show that we belong to this level and we want to increase and take this football club to a different dimension.”

It had been a relatively quiet transfer window for Arsenal, who have recruited just goalkeeper Illan Meslier and winger Christos Tzolis.

However, Arsenal are now moving very bullishly, closing on Newcastle United midfielder Bruno Guimarães, while also targeting Real Madrid’s Vinícius Júnior.

Sam Dean has the full breakdown of a potential deal for the Real Madrid star and how Arsenal are prepared to continue flexing their muscles in the transfer market in what would be one of the biggest moves in Premier League history.

It was January 2025, with Arsenal earning a hard-fought 2-1 comeback victory in the Champions League courtesy of first-half goals from Jorginho and Ethan Nwaneri.

Since this European encounter, Girona have been on a seriously downward trajectory, enduring lowly 16th and 19th finishes in La Liga, with the latter ensuring relegation to the Segunda Division, where they’ll play in the upcoming campaign.

August 5: Arsenal vs Real Betis (Dublin, Ireland)

August 9: Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund (London, England)

August 12: Arsenal vs Como (London, England)

August 16: Arsenal vs Manchester City (Cardiff, Wales)

Mikel Arteta’s side will then begin their defence of the Premier League title on August 21 when they host newly-promoted Coventry City on August 21.

Arsenal are closing in on one of the statement signings of the summer, with Newcastle United midfielder Bruno Guimarães getting closer to joining the Premier League holders.

This deal means that Christian Norgaard is expected to leave and seal a move to Everton for around £7m.

As previously reported by Telegraph Sport, Guimarães has been Arsenal’s top target for weeks. It is believed that he will cost around £80m.

Sam Dean has the full story via this link.

🔵 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 🟡©️ White with the armband✨ Nwaneri floating in the middle🆕 Tzolis from the startAnother pre-season test awaits, LIVE on The Arsenal 📺 Presented by @deel 🤝

Hello and welcome to our live coverage for this pre-season friendly between Girona and Arsenal at Estadi Montilivi in Catalonia.

With the transfer speculation surrounding Vinícius Júnior’s and Bruno Guimaraes’ potential moves to Arsenal ramping up, the reigning Premier League champions are in action against Girona as they step up their preparations ahead of the upcoming campaign.

Unlike other Premier League heavyweights, Arsenal have kept their pre-season tour relatively local with a selection of games in Spain, Ireland and England, before they face Manchester City in the FA Community Shield on August 16 at the Millennium Stadium in Cardiff.

Arsenal beat League One side MK Dons 3-0 in a behind-closed-doors friendly on July 25 at the Sobha Realty Training Centre, thanks to goals from Reiss Nelson, Ethan Nwaneri and Ceadach O’Neill.

After featuring in this victory and setting up Nelson for the opener, Christos Tzolis will be looking to continue his positive momentum with his new club, after joining Arsenal for £34m earlier this summer. Many fans will be keeping a close eye on the recently-signed winger given that various core members of last season’s Premier League-winning squad are yet to return from their post-World Cup breaks, having progressed deep in the competition.

Tournament winners David Raya, Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino, Norway captain Martin Odegaard, as well as England internationals Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke are all missing for this game, while France’s William Saliba is out injured and set for an extended period on the sidelines.

Those who exited the World Cup earlier than the aforementioned players, including Gabriel Magalhaes, Gabriel Martinelli, Piero Hincapie, Kai Havertz, and Viktor Gyokeres, have all joined up with the squad in northern Spain.

Mikel Arteta’s men will play a wounded Girona, who suffered relegation from the top flight of Spanish football last season due to a 19th-place finish.

Kick-off is at 19:00, with team news arriving shortly.

#1847. Stockport County vs Tranmere Rovers - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matthew Cooper | 08 Nov 2026 16:58, Last updated: 08 Nov 2026 17:00

Stockport County will be looking to continue their good form when they welcome Tranmere Rovers to Edgeley Park on Tuesday in the EFL Trophy.

The hosts have already secured their place in the knockout stages, while the visitors could join them with a win.

Stockport currently sit second in League One with 26 points from their opening 14 matches and are among the favourites to earn promotion to the Championship this season.

Jimmy McNulty's side beat Wimbledon 2-1 in their most recent league game, with Jack Diamond and Ethan Ennis scoring in the second half as Stockport came from behind to earn an important win.

The Hatters have also enjoyed an excellent EFL Trophy campaign, recording a 6-3 victory over Everton Under-21s before beating Shrewsbury Town 2-0 to secure their spot in the knockouts.

It is also worth noting that Stockport have only lost to Tranmere twice since 2010, including beating them 3-1 in their most recent meeting in the FA Cup last season.

Tranmere, meanwhile, are 11th in League Two with 19 points from 14 matches and they travel to Greater Manchester following a disappointing FA Cup exit on Saturday.

Darrell Clarke's side were beaten 3-0 by Barnet, with Kane Smith, Nnamdi Oforbh and Damola Ajayi all scoring in the final stages of the game.

However, the Rovers are unbeaten in their last three league games, having picked up a 3-1 win over Cheltenham Town in their most recent fixture.

In the EFL Trophy, Tranmere have only played one game so far, which saw them beat Shrewsbury Town 1-0 thanks to a Dylan Jones strike.

Stockport County form (all competitions):

Luca Ashby-Hammond has been Stockport's EFL Trophy goalkeeper, but he was sent off against Cray Wanderers on Saturday and Oliver Whatmuff is expected to start instead.

Mickael Mandron is likely to start up front, with top scorer Kyle Wootton rested, while Oliver Norwood and Lewis Fiorini are set to continue in midfield.

Tranmere will be hoping top scorer Dylan Jones can continue his good form after he bagged a brace against Cheltenham.

Will Vaulks and Tom Conlon are expected to continue their midfield partnership, while Tom Ince is set to start in the No.10 role.

Stockport County possible starting lineup:

Whatmuff; Dacres-Cogley, Wilson-Brown, Jobe; Ennis, Norwood, Fiorini, Adigun; Glover, Mandron, Wood

Tranmere Rovers possible starting lineup:

McGee; Senior, Faulkner, Nevett, Slater; Conlon, Vaulks; Jones, Ince, Whitaker; Ironside

Stockport are in better form than Tranmere and should have enough quality to pick up the win even if they decide to rotate.

#1846. Virgil van Dijk injury: Liverpool dealt new fitness scare ahead of Manchester United showdown

Virgil van Dijk has withdrawn from the Netherlands squad, potentially making him a doubt for Liverpool’s showdown against Manchester United.

The Liverpool captain had been called up by new Dutch head coach Xavi for the Nations League double-header against Greece and Germany, but it was confirmed on Monday that he - and Sunderland striker Brian Brobbey - have pulled out of the squad.

A statement reads: “Virgil van Dijk and Brian Brobbey have been dropped from the Dutch national team's upcoming international matches. Both players did not return fit from the past weekend's matches and are therefore unavailable.

“The squad thus currently consists of 23 players.”

Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola will be hopeful that Van Dijk’s fitness issue is not too serious as his side’s first game after the November international break is against Man United at Anfield a week on Sunday.

The 35-year-old has continued to be a regular for Liverpool this season, missing just one game so far and starting 14 of his 15 appearances across all competitions.

Van Dijk is not the only Liverpool star not going away for international duty this month after Brazil boss Carlo Ancelotti opted against selecting Alisson Becker for their upcoming friendlies against Japan and Singapore.

Ancelotti said: “We don’t need to test Alisson, we know him very well. He is the best goalkeeper. When the Copa America begins, he will be called up, and it’s the same for the others [experienced players].

“Right now, it’s time to observe, refresh the squad, and help young players reach their full potential.”

#1844. Bompastor: Quick return to action helpful for Chelsea after Everton draw

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Sonia Bompastor believes a quick turnaround following Saturday's disappointing draw with Everton could be a positive thing for Chelsea, ahead of their Champions League meeting with Hacken on Tuesday.

The Blues relinquished top spot in the Women's Super League last weekend as a Lucy Bronze own goal cancelled out Sandy Baltimore's opener at Stamford Bridge.

Chelsea piled on the pressure against opponents who did not manage a single shot on target, firing off 20 attempts of their own, eight of which were on target, and amassing 2.23 expected goals (xG).

But they were unable to avert a 1-1 draw and now sit second in the table behind Manchester City, who trounced West Ham 5-0 on the same day and will be the Blues' next domestic opponents.

But before looking ahead to that top-of-the-table tussle, Bompastor believes having the Hacken fixture come around so quickly offers Chelsea the perfect chance to find their feet again.

"It's important for us to stay in good form, especially on the back of a disappointing result at the weekend," Bompastor said on Monday.

"We also have ambitions in this competition, and right now we are in the top four. That’s the goal: we want to be in the top four and stay there.

"Dropping two points at home is never good, but it happens. The good thing with a quick turnaround is you analyse the game and give the players feedback, but you also need to move on.

"You need to focus on something new. We have a new game coming, in a new competition, so it's the best thing for us in terms of moving on.

"So, we want to put in a good performance and get a good result. Staying strong defensively, not conceding too much and keeping a clean sheet would be a good thing."

Next: Champions League football.  https://t.co/NPEEIxmpP1

— Chelsea FC Women (@ChelseaFCW) November 8, 2026

Chelsea sit fourth in the league-phase table with seven points on the board after three games, with Barcelona, Lyon and Arsenal above them – only the Catalan giants have a perfect record.

Chelsea have lost just one of their 33 group or league-phase games in the Champions League (W24 D8) and are unbeaten across their last 27, since a 4-0 defeat to Wolfsburg in December 2021.

And Hacken's Nordic Wellness Arena holds happy memories for Bompastor, whose first Champions League game as a coach came there with Lyon in October 2021, in a 3-0 win.

Bompastor's 21 Champions League games against teams from outside Europe's big five leagues have yielded 18 wins, three draws, 77 goals scored by her teams, and just 11 conceded.

Naomi Girma and Lauren James are not among Chelsea's travelling squad, but Bompastor confirmed that everyone else is available to face opponents who have only won one of their eight previous home games in the Champions League (D1 L6).

#1843. Three reasons Manchester United have delayed Michael Carrick sack decision after 'crisis talks'

Manchester United are, reportedly, in no rush to make a decision on Michael Carrick’s future, with reasons as to why emerging.

The sack was thought to be looming over Carrick with Man United heading into the November international break sitting in the Premier League relegation zone following a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa on Sunday.

It was then reported by the Overlap that Man Utd’s hierarchy were locked in crisis talks over Carrick’s position.

And now, Sky Sports News have revealed those talks have resulted in a plan for the club’s chiefs to use the international break to fully evaluate the season so far and reassess their options.

While the review will ask how the club - collectively - can quickly reverse their decline, the aforementioned report states there are three key reasons why United are not rushing a decision over the head coach position -

The first reason is Man United supporters are not signing for Carrick being sacked, with the feeling that the pressure for a managerial change which other clubs often experience from the stands has not materialised at Old Trafford.

Secondly, there is a feeling in the boardroom that Carrick and his coaching staff still retain the support of the players.

United snapped a run of nine straight games without a victory by roaring back from 2-0 down to beat Roma 3-2 in the Champions League last week.

They then found themselves two goals down early in both halves against Villa on Sunday, coming back from 2-0 and 4-2 down to salvage a point, and the assessment seems to be that the players are still fighting for Carrick.

Thirdly, and crucially perhaps, United's bosses remain unconvinced at this stage that changing the head coach will solve the team's problems.

Julian Nagelsmann, Eddie Howe, Antonio Conte and Fabian Hurzeler have all been strongly linked as potential replacements for Carrick, while USA manager Mauricio Pochettino has emerged as a surprise late contender.

#1841. Huddersfield Town vs Liverpool Under-21s - prediction, team news, lineups

By Lewis Nolan | 08 Nov 2026 18:18, Last updated: 08 Nov 2026 20:20

Huddersfield Town will look to cement first place in their EFL Trophy clash with visitors Liverpool Under-21s on Tuesday at Accu Stadium.

The Terriers are first with six points in their group and know they will advance into the knockouts, whereas the away side are third with two points and have already been eliminated from the group stage.

Huddersfield are almost certain to claim top spot, as though they are level on points with Doncaster Rovers, they boast a five goal difference advantage with one game left to play, while their rivals' group stage has finished.

In their first two games in the tournament, the Terriers managed to score eight goals, with their latest result in the competition a 5-0 victory against Rochdale on October 6.

Head coach Martin Drury could be forgiven for focusing on League One considering his team are first in the third tier with 29 points from 14 matchweeks and have a strong chance of securing promotion.

The hosts' form of late has been exceptional, as while they lost 2-1 against Exeter City in the FA Cup on Saturday, they had won six and drawn two of their prior eight fixtures.

Huddersfield have failed to claim victory in three of their last five outings at Accu Stadium, though they only suffered one loss in that time.

Liverpool Under-21s know they have finished third in the group given they are four points from second-placed Doncaster Rovers, while they are one point ahead of Rochdale, who have no more fixtures left to play.

The Reds at least come into their next contest on the back of three triumphs from their past five clashes, a period in which they were beaten just once.

Rob Page's side are seventh in the Premier League 2 with 11 points from a possible 18, while they boast a game in hand on five of the teams above them, and a win would see them rise to fourth.

It will concern the head coach that his side have lost three of their six most recent away games, winning just once in that stretch.

In those away contests, Liverpool conceded nine goals and scored six times, and they failed to keep a clean sheet.

Huddersfield Town form (all competitions):

Liverpool Under-21s form (all competitions):

Huddersfield should not risk any of their first-team starters, so perhaps Joe Low and Murray Wallace will partner each other in defence.

Ilias Bronkhorst is dealing with a slight hip issue, though the right-back would not have been in the manager's plans anyway, with Lasse Sorensen a likely inclusion.

Midfielders Ryan Ledson and Ethan Brierley may play behind attacking midfielder David Kasumu, while Samson Tovide is a candidate to lead the line up front.

As for Liverpool, talent Will Wright will hope to be given another chance to impress as the team's striker, though he will need support from Michael Laffey.

Joe Upton and Daniel Onanuga are options for the double pivot ahead of centre-backs Wellity Lucky and Luke Chambers.

Huddersfield Town possible starting lineup:

Alnwick; Sorensen, Low, Wallace, Roughan; Ledson, Brierley; Gooch, Kasumu, Ashia; Tovide

Liverpool Under-21s possible starting lineup:

Davies; O'Connor, Lucky, Chambers, Ayman; Upton, Onanuga; Sonni-Lambie, Laffey, Bradshaw; Wright

Though Huddersfield will be seen as favourites, they are unlikely to take any risks with their lineup on Tuesday.

A weakened XI could give Liverpool Under-21s the edge, though if their recent form is any indicator, an away victory would be narrow.

#1839. Jeglertz expects Man City consistency regardless of Champions League rotation

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Andree Jeglertz wants his Manchester City players to keep imposing their own style of play upon their opponents, even if a packed schedule causes him to rotate his squad in the Champions League this week.

The English champions visit Inter on Tuesday, having thumped West Ham 5-0 last Saturday to overtake Chelsea at the top of the Women's Super League.

City then have a huge clash with Chelsea to come on Saturday, with two further games to play prior to the next international break, away to Hacken in the Champions League and at home to Tottenham in the league.

City have drawn all three of their Champions League games so far this term, with their winless run in the league stage of the competition now stretching back four games (D3 L1), after they won their previous five such matches.

Jeglertz is yet to decide how he will manage his squad over the coming days, but whoever lines up against Inter, he does not expect City's intensity to drop.

"It's only two days between these games and three days to Chelsea," Jeglertz told reporters on Monday.

"So, there are a lot of things to consider; the load for the players, how they recover from that massive game against West Ham, then how we can get the best out of the squad.

"This balance is always something to consider, but we need to figure out how we maintain our way of playing – no matter who we play, we want to play the same way.

"Okay, we play different opponents, but our identity should always be recognised, no matter if it's two days or seven days between games.

"All these games are coming in periods when you play a lot of tight and important matches in the league. The balance for us is to be able to win and get a 90-minute performance at a high level.

"That's what we aim for. There are no guarantees, but the idea and the philosophy is to perform the best we can. That's the target tomorrow, and we'll see how it goes."

City's only previous Champions League meetings with Italian opposition came against Fiorentina in the 2020-21 round of 16, with the English side winning 3-0 at home and 5-0 away.

Despite City's underwhelming European form, striker Khadija Shaw has netted five times in her seven Champions League appearances overall, including scoring in her last two such games.

Only Arsenal's Alessia Russo (17) and Juventus' Alba Redondo (16) have attempted more shots than Shaw (15) in the competition this season.

#1838. 'Standards have fallen': Manchester United fans react to imminent sack decision with Michael Carrick comparison

Manchester United supporters are comparing Michael Carrick’s situation to Pierre Sage as the sack looms for the Crystal Palace boss.

As reported by Standard Sport, Palace’s decision-makers are expected to part ways with the Frenchman heading into the November international break.

The Eagles sunk to the bottom of the Premier League table following Sunday’s 3-1 defeat to Liverpool and have two wins from their opening 10 games.

Man United, meanwhile, are a point and two places above Palace in the relegation zone - but have won just once in the Premier League so far this season, which came against newly-promoted Ipswich in August.

It has seen been reported that the United hierarchy are in no rush to make a decision over Carrick’s future after spirted comebacks against Roma and Aston Villa last week.

The contrast regarding the managerial situations at Old Trafford and Selhurst Park has left some United supporters, on social media, questioning the standards of the club.

One user on X, formerly Twitter, wrote: “Palace are sacking their manager. United still won’t. Reports say Pierre Sage is about to be sacked but Carrick is still being given time.

“United have 8 points, Palace have 7. You’d think Palace were the bigger club.”

Another X user wrote: “Crystal Palace are sitting on 20th and a point behind Manchester United and are looking to SACK their manager Pierre Sage.

“But Manchester United want to keep Michael Carrick. Our standards have truly fallen.”

Carrick inevitably faced more questions about his future immediately following the 4-4 draw against Aston Villa, and he offered an uncharacteristically spiky response during an awkward interview with Patrick Davison on Sky Sports.

He said: “You know the situation, we haven’t won enough games. But I expect to move forward with things we’ve been working on, showing a lot of the good from today, tighten up a few mistakes and win some football matches.”

#1837. Bayern Munich's Harry Kane hailed by German media after Mainz masterclass – "more to his game"

By Matthew Cooper | 08 Nov 2026 18:36, Last updated: 08 Nov 2026 20:48

Harry Kane produced another influential performance for Bayern Munich as the Bundesliga champions maintained their position at the top of the table with a 2-1 victory over Mainz on Saturday.

The England captain assisted both goals as Vincent Kompany's side secured an important three points at the MEWA Arena, with Joshua Kimmich and Lennart Karl finding the back of the net.

Kane first teed up Kimmich in the 14th minute, with the midfielder finding the top corner to give the visitors an early advantage, before setting up Karl in the 57th minute.

Phillip Tietz then scored a consolation goal for the hosts in stoppage time, but Bayern emerged victorious to remain first in the Bundesliga on goal difference.

Harry Kane leading the Bundesliga in assists https://t.co/2iMHUnpU1k

Kane's two assists were particularly significant as they took his tally in the league this season to eight, meaning he has already equalled his best return in a single Bundesliga campaign.

According to Opta, no player has registered more assists during the first nine matchdays of a Bundesliga campaign since they began collecting the data in the 2004-05 season.

Kane is now on course to surpass his best return of 14 assists in a league season, achieved during his final campaign at Tottenham Hotspur in 2020-21, and the German media was full of praise for his performance against Mainz.

Newspaper BILD said he "glänzt diesmal vor allem als Vorbereiter"which means that Kane "shone primarily as a provider".

However, they also noted that "the only thing missing for the Ballon d'Or winner was a goal of his own", with Kane failing to score in his last four games across all competitions for Bayern.

T-online, meanwhile, wrote that Kane "impressed with his excellent vision, ability to switch play, and passing" but that he was "unlucky with his own finishing".

The official Bundesliga website wrote an article titled "Bayern Munich's Harry Kane shows there is more to his game in Mainz win".

The piece stated that Kane's return in front of goal has been "slightly below his admittedly high standards", but stated that he "remains directly involved in Bayern’s success on the pitch" and that it was "no surprise Bayern were eager to offer him a new contract".

???? ?? ?????! ? +? ? 90'+3 | #M05FCB | 1-2 ⬜ https://t.co/MK7PLP8RrO

Kane will be keen to get back to his best in front of goal, but it is great to see him demonstrating his value in other ways after extending his stay at Bayern until 2029.

Kimmich highlighted this fact after the win over Mainz, stating: "He set up both goals today, and he also set one up against Atletico Madrid.

"He's always heavily involved, and even when he doesn't set any goals up, he's still very important for our game because - his goals aside - he has qualities we really need."

The 33-year-old remains one of Europe's most prolific goalscorers, having bagged 10 goals in 15 games across all competitions so far, but his ability to create opportunities for teammates has become an increasingly important part of his game.

Bayern will be back in action next weekend when they host Koln and it will be very interesting to see what impact Kane has on that game.

#1836. FA Cup draw in full: Second round fixtures confirmed as Leyton Orient and non-league sides learn fate

Wimborne Town will face Bradford in the second round of the FA Cup, while Leicester have been handed an away tie against lower league opposition.

Seventh-tier Wimborne are one of the lowest-ranked teams left in this season’s competition after causing a major upset in round one by beating League Two strugglers Crawley Town.

As such, the Magpies’ reward is another home tie in the second round as they have drawn League One side Bradford - who will face Manchester City in the Carabao Cup quarter-final.

Leicester, the 2021 winners, must overcome non-league opposition in Dover Athletic to reach the third round, while Leyton Orient will face last season’s quarter-finalists in Port Vale.

Elsewhere, 2013 winners Wigan take on Barnsley in an all-League One showdown and Jack Wilshere’s Luton Town have been handed a trip to AFC Fylde.

Plymouth Parkway have overcome Berkhamsted after extra-time in the final first round tie and will be at home in round two against Barnet.

FA Cup second round ties will be held across and around the weekend of December 5, 2026.
